sections.title: What Novis claims
sections.blurb: Who the language is for, the three things it promises, and the ordering that decides every trade below.

rules.title: Novis is built for web applications of every kind, with command-line tooling second
Novis claims three things, and "faster than PHP" is not one of them
The PHP-shaped syntax is an on-ramp, and no document may promise compatibility
rules.diverges: existing PHP packages, frameworks and code do not run, and no document may imply otherwise

rules.title: When two slices compete, the one that gets a working application sooner wins
Memory buys security, correctness, latency and simplicity — bounded, attributable and stated

sections.title: Names, files and programs
sections.blurb: How a name reaches the file that declares it — while compiling, with no loader running anywhere.

rules.title: `Core\Program::implementing<T>()` lists every concrete class that is a `T`, for an interface or a class, and it expands while compiling
rules.diverges: a plugin roster is a compile-time array literal, not a `foreach` over `new $className`

rules.title: `Core\Program::implementingWith<I, T>($member)` joins the enumeration with one attribute per class, and it expands while compiling
rules.diverges: a plugin roster with its metadata is one compile-time array literal, not a `ReflectionClass` sweep over discovered classes

rules.title: `Core\Program::constructors<T, C>()` lists the enumeration's classes with one closure each, typed by `C`, and it expands while compiling
rules.diverges: a plugin factory list is a compile-time array literal of closures, not `new $className(...$args)` over discovered names

rules.title: A compile target changes the host context, never the language
A name reaches its file while compiling; there is no runtime loader of any kind
rules.diverges: there is no `spl_autoload_register`, no `__autoload` and no `new $name` — a name held in a string can never reach a file

rules.title: `autoload` maps a prefix to roots, resolved relative to the file that declares it
rules.diverges: the map is a declaration in source rather than a registered loader or a `psr-4` manifest, and it travels with the code instead of with the deployment

rules.title: A file reached by autoload declares exactly one thing, under the name the map finds it by
rules.diverges: PSR-4 imposes this by convention; here it is a diagnostic

rules.title: A `require` path is compared against the on-disk entry exactly, on every OS
rules.diverges: `require` does not inherit the filesystem's case behaviour, so a path that resolves on Windows or macOS resolves on Linux or fails on all three

rules.title: A relative path literal at a path parameter names a file beside the source file that wrote it, and a relative path built at run time throws
rules.diverges: PHP resolves a relative `fopen` path against the process's working directory; here a literal resolves against its own source file, and nothing resolves against the working directory implicitly

rules.title: `Core\Program::id()` is 64 hex characters naming this program's code and environment
A bundled executable is one trust domain: a program, never a service

sections.title: The first-party framework
sections.blurb: Novis ships the framework, split into a privileged half in the binary and an opinionated half as a package.

rules.title: Novis ships the framework, split by the standard-library placement tests
The privileged half of the framework is `Core`, compiled into the binary
The opinionated half is `nvs/web`, a first-party package providing the `Web` namespace
The framework has no ORM, no runtime container, and no second way to do anything
rules.diverges: the ORM, the service container, the facade, the route cache and the autoload dump have no equivalent, and each is absent by construction rather than by omission

rules.title: No migration runner ships until migration semantics are decided
`nvs new` writes an application that runs before it is edited

sections.title: Declarations and numbers
sections.blurb: Every binding declares its type and keeps it. The numeric tower, its one implicit conversion, and what overflow does.

rules.title: Every binding declares its type, and no binding's type ever changes
rules.diverges: a local, a `foreach` binding, a `for` counter and a destructuring target all carry a type, written or (for the first three) taken with `var`, and PHP source with neither does not compile

rules.title: `var` takes a local's or a `foreach` binding's type from the expression that fills it, and fixes it there for good
The type grammar is a closed set of atoms under unions and intersections
An integer literal is decimal, `0x`, `0o` or `0b`, and a leading zero is not a radix
rules.diverges: `017` is decimal seventeen where PHP reads octal fifteen; PHP's leading-zero octal is refused rather than reinterpreted

rules.title: A numeric literal is untyped until it is placed, and `as T` is a placing position
rules.diverges: a fractional literal is not born a `float` — `decimal $price = 19.99;` is exact — and there is no literal suffix for any numeric type

rules.title: `uint` is a distinct unsigned 64-bit integer, and it costs no bytes a value did not already hold
rules.diverges: PHP has one integer type; Novis has two, told apart by `Core\Reflect::typeOf` and by `$x is uint` (`rule:types/type-test`), so a value PHP's `is_int()` accepted answers `is uint` and not `is int`, and the whole 64-bit range is representable

rules.title: An arithmetic operator answers in its operands' own type, and overflow throws rather than wrapping or promoting
rules.diverges: `PHP_INT_MAX + 1` throws `ArithmeticError` instead of becoming a `float`, `int` against `uint` does not compile, and a `bool`, `string`, `array<T>` or object operand has no `+` at all

rules.title: An `int` or `uint` widening into a `float` position is the only implicit conversion in the language
rules.diverges: the widening throws above 2^53 instead of rounding, and no other implicit coercion survives

rules.title: `decimal` is an exact scalar of 96 mantissa bits and a scale of 0 to 28
rules.diverges: `bcmath` and `gmp` are retired rather than ported — exact fractional arithmetic is a register-sized scalar, and arbitrary-magnitude integers are `Core\BigInt`

sections.title: Text, bytes and literal types
sections.blurb: A string is UTF-8 for its whole lifetime, bytes is its unencoded peer, and a literal can be a type of its own.

rules.title: Only the types the table orders may be ordered, and two objects need `Comparable`
rules.diverges: there is no fallback ordering — PHP orders anything by converting an operand first, and Novis refuses a `string`, `bytes`, `array<T>`, `callable`, enum case or `null` operand where it is written

rules.title: A `string` is valid UTF-8 for its whole lifetime, and its unmarked unit is the grapheme cluster
rules.diverges: `strlen` counts bytes and needs `mb_strlen` plus a correct ambient encoding to count characters; a Novis `string` has one encoding and one length, counting extended grapheme clusters unconditionally

rules.title: `bytes` is a primitive peer to `string` for data that carries no encoding
rules.diverges: PHP has one type for text and for a buffer and never says which a value is; a request body, a socket read, a file's contents and a digest all arrive as `bytes` and become text only by a conversion that can throw

rules.title: `1h30m` is a `Core\Time\Duration` constant, in one grammar shared by source, `parse` and `nvs.toml`
A `string` or `int` literal is its own type, and a union of them is a closed set
A scalar class constant used as a type folds to its own literal type
An enum case used as a type is a narrowed subtype of its enum, never its backing integer

sections.title: Arrays and property keys
sections.blurb: PHP's ordered hash with a declared element type, and the type whose values are a class's own property names.

rules.title: An array is PHP's ordered hash with `string` keys and a declared element type
rules.diverges: there is no integer key — `Core\Arr::keys()` returns `array<string>` and a `foreach` key binds as a `string` — and an element type is declared and enforced on every write, reading covariantly

rules.title: Three combining members treat every key alike, and `array + array` does not compile
rules.diverges: there is no `merge` under any spelling and no array `+` operator; `array_merge`'s rule chosen by a key's type does not survive a language where every key is a `string`

rules.title: `{preserveKeys: false}` discards every key, whatever shape the key has
rules.diverges: PHP renumbers integer keys and silently keeps string ones; `false` means the result is a list, and nothing else

rules.title: A subscript through a `mixed` is the tag's question; every other base answers it where it is written
rules.diverges: a read that finds no array and no key is a catchable throw, never PHP's warning and a `null`

rules.title: `property<T>` is a type whose values are `T`'s public property names, and `as` is its only source
`property<T>` widens as `T` narrows, because the argument bounds the receiver
`$obj->$key` accepts a `property<T>` and nothing else; a read is the union and a write is checked
rules.diverges: a computed property name is not a string at the site — every other operand is refused, dispatch through a computed *method* name stays refused, and a `readonly` field in the set is refused at the write

sections.title: Unions, narrowing and conversion
sections.blurb: What a union permits, the four spellings of narrowing, and the single conversion operator that replaced the cast.

rules.title: A union permits only what every member permits, and `mixed` is the one position checked nowhere
rules.diverges: there is no `is_int()`-style free function to narrow with — the question is the `is` operator (`rule:types/type-test`) — and `mixed` never absorbs implicitly: `int $n = $m;` is a diagnostic rather than a runtime check

rules.title: `$x is T` tests whether a value holds a `T`, answers `bool`, and never refuses because the answer is knowable
rules.diverges: `int` and `uint` are separate tags, so a `BIGINT UNSIGNED` value answers `is uint` and not `is int` where `is_int()` was true for both, and `string` and `bytes` are separate the same way; `is 3.14` is refused outright, there being no float literal type

rules.title: Narrowing is flow-sensitive and branch-local, and there are exactly four spellings of it
`expr as T` is the only conversion, and it produces a `T` or throws
rules.diverges: nothing converts silently — `(int)"abc"` is not `0`, `PHP_INT_MAX + 1` is not a `float`, and `settype` does not exist; every conversion is written, checked, and throws rather than substituting

rules.title: PHP's `(T)expr` cast does not parse, and the diagnostic names the `as` that replaces it
rules.diverges: `(int)`, `(uint)`, `(float)`, `(string)`, `(bool)`, `(array)` and `(object)` are all parse errors rather than a second spelling of `as`

rules.title: A `type` alias is a transparent, compile-time-only synonym for a type expression
A `type` alias may not name a single bare class
A `type` alias is also a member of a class, interface or enum, reached as `Owner::Name` and as a bare `Name` inside its owner

sections.title: Closures and callables
sections.blurb: One closure literal, one callable type, capture by value with no `use` clause, and the variance that follows.

rules.title: `callable` is satisfied by a closure and by nothing else, and no object is callable
rules.diverges: PHP's bare-name string, `"Class::method"` string and `[$obj, 'method']` array are all refused, and `__invoke` has no meaning — `$obj(...)` is a diagnostic whatever the class declares

rules.title: `fn` is the only closure literal, with an expression body or a block body
rules.diverges: `function (...) {...}` and `function (...) use (...) {...}` do not parse at all; `fn` gains the block body PHP's arrow form never had

rules.title: A `callable` type may name its parameters, and must then name its return type
A closure satisfies a callable type when its arity is at most the type's, matched from the left
A callable's parameters are contravariant and its return type covariant
An unannotated `fn` parameter takes its type from the position the literal is written in
`callable` is the only closure type name, and a callable value is invoked directly
rules.diverges: there is no `Closure` type, no `Closure::fromCallable`, and no `call_user_func`/`call_user_func_array`

rules.title: A closure captures by value exactly the outer names its body reads, and there is no `use` clause
rules.diverges: capture is never written, and `use (&$y)` has no replacement — a shared mutable cell is an ordinary object in user code

rules.title: A closure may carry a self-name, visible only inside its own body

sections.title: Objects, shapes and class references
sections.blurb: The opaque top of every class type, anonymous object literals, structural shapes, and a class as a value.

rules.title: `object` is the opaque top of every class type
`{name: value}` builds an anonymous, methodless object and nothing more
rules.diverges: there is no shorthand `{x, y}` and no computed key, so no path leads back to PHP's dynamic properties

rules.title: `{name: T}` in type position is a structural shape checked by width subtyping, and `{name?: T}` marks a key that may be absent
A member reached through an erased receiver is answered at run time, and a failure is a throw
rules.diverges: a missing name, a wrong-typed write and a receiver holding no object are all catchable throws, never a warning plus a `null`, and a write can never create a field

rules.title: `class<T>` is a type whose value is a class descriptor, and `as` is its only source
`class<T>` widens wherever `T` widens, and never narrows without an `as`
Three sites accept a `class<T>`, and every other operand is still refused there
`::class` answers the class the value is, and folding is an optimization of that
rules.diverges: `$m::class` on a `mixed` is refused where it is written rather than failing at run time; narrow the receiver first, the way `->` already requires

sections.title: Truthiness and equality
sections.blurb: Six positions test truthiness and every other bool stays checked; one equality operator, with one row per type.

rules.title: Six syntax positions test truthiness; every other `bool` position stays checked
rules.diverges: the implicit conversion to `bool` is confined to six positions, where PHP applies it wherever a `bool` is wanted

rules.title: The truthy table is PHP's, and `bytes` is falsy only when it is empty
rules.diverges: `bytes` has no PHP neighbour and takes emptiness alone, so a one-octet `"0"` buffer is truthy where the string `"0"` is falsy

rules.title: `and`, `or` and `xor` do not parse, and `&&`/`||` are the whole set
rules.diverges: the low-precedence keyword connectives are gone entirely, and `xor` has no operator replacement at all

rules.title: A `?T` used directly as a condition is warned about, not refused
`==` and `!=` are the whole of equality, and `===`, `!==` and `<>` do not parse
rules.diverges: there is no loose-versus-strict pair to pick between — one operator, which never converts either operand

rules.title: Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading
rules.diverges: each row where PHP's two operators disagreed takes `===`'s answer — two strings compare as text and never as numbers, and an array compares in key order

rules.title: A `mixed` or union operand resolves at run time, and a mismatched pair answers `false`
rules.diverges: a cross-type pairing is `false` rather than PHP's converting comparison, and it is the one place a comparison answers instead of refusing to compile

rules.title: Two objects are equal only when they are the same object, and no class may change that
rules.diverges: PHP's `==` walked properties; here there is no property walk, no `__equals`, no `equals()` protocol and no `Equatable` interface

rules.title: Comparing two types that no single value inhabits is a compile error
rules.diverges: `"1" == 1` neither answers `true` nor `false`; it does not compile, and the diagnostic names the conversion the author meant

rules.title: A `switch` label and a `match` arm compare by the equality rule and by nothing else
rules.diverges: `switch` no longer compares loosely while `match` compares identically — there is one comparison, and both use it

sections.title: Conversion and the intrinsics
sections.blurb: The failable conversion that answers null instead of throwing, and what the compiler prepares from a literal argument.

rules.title: A literal argument to an intrinsic `Core` call is validated while checking and prepared into the artifact
rules.diverges: a malformed pattern, URI, duration or format string is a compile error at the offset inside the literal, rather than a throw on the first request that reaches the call

rules.title: The intrinsic roster is a closed set in the compiler's own source, and nothing declares itself into it
`list(...)` does not parse; `[...]` is the only destructuring target
rules.diverges: one of PHP's two destructuring spellings is refused, so `list($a, $b) = $pair;` is a diagnostic naming the bracket form

rules.title: `??+=`, `??-=` and `??.=` are `$a = ($a ?? d) op $v` with the target evaluated once and `d` the zero of the target's type
rules.diverges: PHP has none of the three operators; its `$a[$k]++` and `$a[$k] .= $s` on an absent key read it as `null` with a warning

rules.title: `expr as ?T` yields the converted value or `null`, and never throws
rules.diverges: a failed conversion is a `null` the caller tests, where `(int)$x` — which does not parse at all — answered `0` and said nothing

rules.title: `as ?T` is refused where the conversion cannot fail, where none exists, and at every class target
rules.diverges: there is no operator downcast: `$s as ?Core\Uri` is a compile error rather than a cast, and text reaches a class only through that class's own reader

rules.title: `as ?T` decides `tainted` and `secret` by exactly the rule `as T` uses, and launders nothing of its own
A failable single-`string` parse is spelled `tryParse`, and no separate validity predicate stands beside it
rules.diverges: no validator sits next to a parser the way `filter_var` sits next to `parse_url`; `tryParse` is `parse` with the throw caught, so the two can never read one string differently

rules.title: The prepared path and the runtime path are one implementation, so preparation is only earlier and never different

sections.title: The pipeline and the catch expression
sections.blurb: Two constructs PHP has no spelling for: a parse-time substitution, and a typed catch that guards one expression.

rules.title: `|>` substitutes one hole at parse time, and has no run-time representation
rules.diverges: PHP 8.5's `|>` applies a callable resolved at run time; this one substitutes `$_` in the parser, so the emitted tree is the nested spelling's and no closure is allocated

rules.title: `|>` binds tighter than every binary operator and looser than unary
The hole is `$_`, it appears exactly once on a right side, and nowhere else at all
An expression-level `catch` is a chain of typed arms guarding one expression
rules.diverges: PHP has no expression-level `catch`; a one-line fallback for a throwing call is a language form rather than a swallowed `@` or a five-line block

rules.title: `catch` sits between assignment and the ternary, so one arm guards a whole `??` chain
An arm body is an expression, which admits `throw` and refuses `return` by name
The result type is the union of the guard and every arm, and an arm is checked from the pre-guard state
An unbound `catch (Throwable)` arm that supplies a value is warned about
rules.diverges: PHP's `@` is gone, and the one-liner that would regrow it is named at compile time instead

rules.title: The expression form lowers to the block form's landing pad, with the value in a temporary
`Name(...)` is the only spelling that takes a reference to a declared member

sections.title: Names, namespaces and `require`
sections.blurb: One function decides what every name means, nothing gets a second name, and `require` is the only inclusion construct.

rules.title: `<?nvs` is the only code-mode open tag; `<?php` is refused
rules.diverges: a file opening with `<?php` reports a diagnostic, though the code after the tag still parses

rules.title: A name containing a separator is read from the root, and one without it through the imports
rules.diverges: a relative qualified name (`Models\User` inside `namespace App;`) names nothing, and a namespace-prefix import reaches nothing under it

rules.title: A short name resolves through the imports and then the enclosing namespace, and stops
rules.diverges: there is no fallback to the root namespace, so a namespaced file that catches writes `use Throwable;`

rules.title: A leading separator does not parse, in any of the three positions PHP writes one
rules.diverges: `\App\Models\User`, `use \App\Models\User;` and `namespace \App;` are each refused rather than accepted and ignored

rules.title: One function decides what a name means, and there is no second place that does
A declaration is reachable under exactly the name it was declared with
rules.diverges: `use Foo\Bar as Baz;` is a diagnostic, and no function anywhere registers a second name for a class

rules.title: An enum's name is an ordinary type, usable at every binding site a class name is
`require` is the only file-inclusion construct, and it runs every time it is reached
rules.diverges: `include`, `include_once` and `require_once` are parse-time refusals — there is no warn-and-continue and no repeat guard

rules.title: Declarations cross a `require` and variables do not
rules.diverges: an included file cannot see the includer's locals, and the includer cannot see its own

rules.title: A `require` used for its value hands back `mixed`, and converts like any other boundary

sections.title: Where state lives
sections.blurb: A program holds state in five declared places. There is no `global`, no function static, and no host-populated variable.

rules.title: `static` marks a class member and names a class-relative type, and nothing else
rules.diverges: `self::m()` and `parent::m()` inside a closure set the called class to the class the closure is written in, where PHP forwards the enclosing method's called class; `self::m()` in a method body on an `abstract static` `m` runs the subclass's body, where PHP throws

rules.title: A function holds no state of its own, and `global` does not exist
rules.diverges: `static int $calls = 0;` inside a function and `global $x;` are both parse-time refusals, each naming a class static, a constant or a parameter as the replacement

rules.title: A program holds state in five declared places, and the list is closed
rules.diverges: there is no global constant and no superglobal, so nothing holds state without a declaration a reader can find

rules.title: An isolate's class statics are its own, and a child cannot reach its parent's
No variable is ever populated by the host; every superglobal is a `Core` class member
rules.diverges: `$_SERVER`, `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_COOKIE`, `$_FILES`, `$_SESSION`, `$_ENV`, `$argv` and `$argc` do not exist as variables at all

rules.title: `$GLOBALS` and `$_REQUEST` have no replacement of any kind
rules.diverges: neither gets a `Core` class, so `extract($_GET)`-shaped code has no straight-line conversion

rules.title: A closure binds `$this` only when its body names it, so `static fn` has nothing left to assert
rules.diverges: a closure that never names `$this` is unbound, and `bindTo()`/`bind()` on it return an equivalent closure rather than rebinding anything

sections.title: By-reference and termination
sections.blurb: A by-reference binding is written `inout` and said again at the call site; `&` does not parse and `die` is refused.

rules.title: A by-reference binding is written `inout`, in the modifier slot before the type
rules.diverges: `&$x` is not a by-reference marker; the word is `inout` and it goes before the type

rules.title: An argument that binds an `inout` parameter says so at the call
rules.diverges: PHP removed call-time by-reference in 5.4 and left the caller no marker at all; here the marker is mandatory in both directions

rules.title: An `inout` argument is a local, and never an element or a property
There is no write-only `out` mode
`&` in a by-reference position is refused at parse time
rules.diverges: `&` keeps only bitwise AND, logical AND and the intersection type; every by-reference spelling of it is a diagnostic

rules.title: `exit` is the only process-termination keyword; `die` is refused
rules.diverges: `die` and `die('bye')` do not compile; `exit` is the exact replacement

sections.title: Declaring a class
sections.blurb: Everything lives in a class body. Constructors, promotion, and the proof that every property is assigned before it is read.

rules.title: No `function` and no `const` may be declared outside a class body
rules.diverges: a global function or a global constant cannot be declared at all — every callable is a method, every constant a class constant, and there is no exception for built-ins

rules.title: Every name is compared exactly, so `Foo` and `foo` are two names and never one
rules.diverges: class, interface and method names no longer fold case, so a mis-cased reference is a diagnostic instead of a silent match

rules.title: Keywords, contextual keywords and the `<?nvs` tag are lower case and nothing else
rules.diverges: `IF`, `TRUE` and `NULL` are not keywords or literals — they lex as ordinary identifiers, and only `<?NVS` gets a diagnostic of its own

rules.title: No property, parameter or local name may begin with `_`
rules.diverges: PHP's `_private` and `$_unused` conventions do not compile; there is no leading-underscore allowance in any identifier category

rules.title: A constructor is an ordinary method named `constructor`, and `__construct` does not compile
rules.diverges: the constructor is spelled `constructor`; `__construct` is refused where it is written, with a diagnostic naming the rename

rules.title: A visibility keyword on a parameter promotes it to a property only in the `constructor`
A `new` through a class reference checks `T`'s constructor, and an implementor whose constructor diverges is refused there
rules.diverges: the mismatch is refused at the `new` rather than discovered when the wrong subclass arrives

rules.title: Every property a class declares is definitely assigned on every path out of every constructor
rules.diverges: a constructor that leaves a typed property unset on some path is refused at compile time rather than throwing at whichever read discovers it

rules.title: There is no `undefined`: a property that may legitimately hold no value is `?T`
Reading a property that has never been written throws a catchable error and never yields a value

sections.title: Properties, hooks and observers
sections.blurb: `lateinit` for what the constructor cannot fill, hooks for what a read or write should run, and an interface where PHP had `__get`.

rules.title: A `lateinit` property is assigned after the constructor rather than inside it
`lateinit` is admitted only on a non-nullable class- or interface-typed property that is neither promoted nor `readonly`
A `lateinit` read the enclosing method can prove is too early is a compile error, and nothing wider is attempted
A property that the class does not declare cannot be read or written, and no user code runs for the attempt
rules.diverges: there are no dynamic properties and no `__get`/`__set` to catch one — a wrong name is a diagnostic or a checked throw, never a newly created field

rules.title: `unset` on a declared property is a compile error, and `isset` on one is an ordinary null test
rules.diverges: `unset($obj->prop)` does not remove a property — the one surviving operand is an array element

rules.title: A property's own `get`/`set` hook is PHP 8.4's, unchanged, and every read or write of that property is a call to it
A class observes every read and write of its own properties by implementing `PropertyObserver`, never by declaring `__get`/`__set`
rules.diverges: `__get`/`__set` are not recognized by name; observation is a declared `implements` that sees every property, not an ambient fallback that sees only the undefined ones

rules.title: A property access runs its hook or its storage first and the observer second, and the observer cannot change the answer
A class that implements no `PropertyObserver` pays nothing for one

sections.title: Interfaces and delegation
sections.blurb: There is no `trait`: shared behaviour is a default method, and shared state is a field you delegate to.

rules.title: A member reachable from two default or delegated sources with no override is a compile error
rules.diverges: there is no `insteadof`; the only way to pick a winner is an ordinary override that calls the source it wants by name

rules.title: There is no `trait`: shared behaviour is an interface method with a body, shared state is `by` delegation
rules.diverges: `trait`, a class-body `use Trait;` and `insteadof` are not in the grammar at all

rules.title: A `public` interface method with a body is a default method, and `$this` inside it is the interface
A `private` interface method is visible only to that interface's own bodies
An interface declares no property: one written there is `E0254`, and the value comes from a method or a constant
rules.diverges: 8.4 admits a hooked property in an interface; Novis admits no property there at all

rules.title: `implements I by $field` forwards every member `I` requires to that property

sections.title: Behaviour is declared, never magic
sections.blurb: No method changes a class by being present. Ordering, string conversion and dumping each go through a named interface.

rules.title: Two objects order only when their class implements `Comparable`, and there is no property-walk fallback
rules.diverges: PHP's recursive property-by-property comparison of two same-class objects does not exist; ordering an unorderable pair is a compile error rather than an ambient walk

rules.title: `compareTo` fixes the other operand to `self`, so two different classes are never ordered against each other
rules.diverges: two objects of different classes are a compile error rather than a comparison PHP answers by falling through its own coercion rules

rules.title: `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` and `<=>` on two objects lower to one `compareTo` call
An object becomes a string only through `Stringable::toString`, and everywhere else is a diagnostic
rules.diverges: `__toString` is not recognized; the capability is `implements Stringable` and its absence is refused where the object is rendered

rules.title: No method name changes a class's behaviour by being present; every PHP magic method is replaced by a declared interface or gone
rules.diverges: a double-underscore method name is refused where it is written, so no class can declare a hook the runtime would call on its own

rules.title: There is no `__call` or `__callStatic`: a call to a method the class does not declare is a diagnostic
rules.diverges: dispatch to an undeclared method name does not exist in any form, and the two names cannot even be written down

rules.title: There are no destructors: cleanup is an explicit method call the holder makes
rules.diverges: `__destruct` does not exist in any form, and nothing user-declared runs when a refcount reaches zero

rules.title: A debug dump shows a class's real declared properties and their real values, and no class can change that
rules.diverges: `__debugInfo` does not exist, so a dump cannot be filtered, renamed or synthesized by the class being dumped

sections.title: Copying and serializing
sections.blurb: Two copy depths, neither of which a class customizes, and a serialization format closed to everything it did not write.

rules.title: A copy is either `clone`'s one level or the graph copy, and no class customizes either
rules.diverges: `__clone`, `__serialize`, `__unserialize`, `__sleep` and `__wakeup` do not exist, so a copy always means what the language says it means

rules.title: `clone` copies an object's declared storage one level deep and shares every object it reaches
The graph copy is one recursive, cycle-safe walk with two carriers, and it refuses what has no meaning on the other side
`Core\Serialize::decode` accepts only bytes this build's `encode` produced, and refuses everything else outright
rules.diverges: PHP's open, cross-version `serialize` wire format is not readable, and no hook fires during reconstruction, so the object-injection class has nothing to drive

rules.title: Every encoder that walks a value graph ends a cycle by identity and names the path, never by exhausting a depth cap
rules.diverges: `json_encode` reports a recursive reference by returning `false` and setting `JSON_ERROR_RECURSION`, and names no path; here the encoder throws and the message carries the property chain that closed the cycle

rules.title: A class is reachable under its declared name and nowhere else
rules.diverges: `class_alias` does not exist and will not be added, so no class ever answers to a second runtime-reachable name

sections.title: Enums
sections.blurb: An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type — and costs nothing beyond the integer it is.

rules.title: A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero
rules.diverges: every case has an integer value even where none is written, so PHP's valueless pure case does not exist

rules.title: PHP's `case` keyword does not parse, and each one is diagnosed where it is written
rules.diverges: `case Hearts = 1;` is not a spelling this language has — an enum body is a comma list

rules.title: An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type
rules.diverges: an enum is not a class in disguise — a case is a compile-time constant, with no singleton, no allocation and no identity

rules.title: Every enum is backed by exactly one integer type, and nothing else backs one
rules.diverges: there is no pure enum and no `string`-backed enum, and `BackedEnum` and `UnitEnum` do not exist

rules.title: An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is
rules.diverges: a case is a scalar, so it copies across an isolate boundary like an `int` and has no identity to preserve

rules.title: An enum case is always truthy, whatever integer backs it
A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases
rules.diverges: no methods, no interfaces, no enum constants, and no `::cases()`, `::from()`, `::tryFrom()`, `->value` or `->name`

rules.title: Reflection describes an enum's shape and grants it nothing a class has
rules.diverges: there are no case instances for a description to hand back — it carries the type's name and its case list, and nothing that acts

sections.title: Iteration
sections.blurb: What `for` and `foreach` drive, the two interfaces that carry every iteration, and what a generator is and is not.

rules.title: A `for` init clause is one typed declaration or a list of expressions, never both
A header-declared counter is function-scoped, and a second header declaring it again is refused
A refused `for` header is one diagnostic, never a cascade
`foreach` drives exactly three subjects, and a fourth is refused where it is written
rules.diverges: an object is iterable only by declaring `Iterable<T>` or `Iterator<T>`; walking an ordinary object's public properties does not compile

rules.title: Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is `advance()` then `current()`
rules.diverges: no `rewind()`, `key()`, `valid()` or `IteratorAggregate`, and none of the ~20 SPL iterator classes; a cursor has two members and no key half

rules.title: A class implements a compiler-owned generic interface at a concrete type, and declares no type variable of its own
A class cannot make `$obj[$k]` or a count into a method call
rules.diverges: `ArrayAccess` and `Countable` do not exist; a collection exposes `->get($k)`, `->set($k, $v)` and `->count()` instead

rules.title: `current()` outside the protocol throws rather than answering
rules.diverges: reading a cursor before it has advanced, or after it is drained, is an error rather than a `null` or a stale element

rules.title: A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it
rules.diverges: a generator is a compiled state machine rather than a suspended stack, so it costs one small object and behaves the same on every compile target

rules.title: A generator is a lazy sequence and nothing more
rules.diverges: no `yield from`, no `send()`, no `throw()` into a generator, no keyed `yield`, and no generator return value to retrieve

rules.title: `yield` appears only in the generator's own body
rules.diverges: a helper called from a generator cannot yield into it; delegation is written as a `foreach` that re-yields

rules.title: A generator does not cross a boundary and does not clone

sections.title: Attributes
sections.blurb: An attribute is a shape literal on a declaration — inert data from the moment it is parsed, matched by shape rather than by name.

rules.title: An attribute is a shape literal on a declaration, and nothing is ever declared or instantiated for it
rules.diverges: an attribute is never an object — PHP builds a real one the first time `ReflectionAttribute::newInstance()` is called, and needs a declared `#[Attribute]` class for every attribute kind

rules.title: An attribute attaches at four declaration sites, and a named one's name is a shape-typed `type` alias
rules.diverges: a named attribute resolves to a `type` alias rather than to a class, so there is no per-attribute-kind declaration and no second namespace of attribute names

rules.title: Every field value in an attribute payload is a compile-time constant
rules.diverges: PHP admits any expression as an attribute argument, `new` included, so building one has an execution order and side effects

rules.title: An attribute may be attached to one declaration any number of times, and attach time never counts them
rules.diverges: repeatability is the default and needs no `Attribute::IS_REPEATABLE` marker

rules.title: An explicit `<T>` at a call site is written for compiler-owned members only
rules.diverges: `Foo::BAR < X > ($y)` reads as a call carrying a type argument where PHP reads two comparisons

rules.title: A retrieval matches a payload by the shape it satisfies, never by the name it was attached under
rules.diverges: there is no `ReflectionAttribute` and no lookup by attribute class name; two unrelated libraries can ask for the same shape without agreeing on a name

rules.title: A retrieval is answered while checking and replaced by its answer, so ambiguity is a compile error
rules.diverges: "which one did I get?" for a repeated attribute is a diagnostic at the call site rather than a question a test run answers, and no reflection table reaches the compiled unit

rules.title: `#[Api]` may add to the generated document and may not contradict the code
rules.diverges: an annotation that disagrees with the handler is a compile error rather than a documentation bug nobody notices

rules.title: A method carrying `#[Route]` carries `#[Access]`, and an omission does not compile
rules.diverges: no PHP framework can refuse to build a route whose author wrote no access decision

rules.title: `#[Access]` names one resolvable decision in `allow`, and one of them covers a method

sections.title: How an error travels
sections.blurb: A throw is a checked return, not an unwind. What that buys, what it costs, and how deep recursion is allowed to go.

rules.title: A limit report is not a Throwable, and the type checker knows it
rules.diverges: `catch (Throwable)` provably cannot see a resource-limit fatal; `Exception` and `Error` are not class names

rules.title: An error propagates as a checked return, never by unwinding
rules.diverges: an exception is a status value checked after every call, not a stack unwind

rules.title: A throw costs no more than a return, and only its raise allocates
rules.diverges: throwing is not a performance cliff, so exceptions may be used on ordinary control-flow paths

rules.title: A runtime helper never unwinds, and a panic dies inside one request
Recursion is bounded twice: a catchable error, then a fatal
rules.diverges: recursion is bounded by an 8 MB native stack rather than by `memory_limit`, so deep PHP recursion needs a rewrite

sections.title: The escalation ladder
sections.blurb: Four tiers between a failing request and a dead server, none of them retried, ending at a native floor that gives up.

rules.title: Tier 1 — a resource limit reaches the request that spent it
rules.diverges: the handler is request-local rather than global, and runs on a reserve carved out before execution started

rules.title: An allocation past the memory ceiling is refused before it is made, and the refusal is a complete no-op
A failure escalates through four tiers, and no tier is retried
rules.diverges: every failure category ends in a log line, and no handler is ever given a second attempt at the same failure

rules.title: Tier 2 — an uncaught throw reaches the request root as itself
rules.diverges: the handler is request-local and fires exactly once; there is no global `set_exception_handler`

rules.title: Tier 3 — the configured handler is an ordinary isolate on the engine's own budget
Tier 4 — the floor is native, bounded, and gives up rather than escalating
An internal panic never runs the failing request's own code
A compile failure is catchable mid-execution and reaches the ladder at entry

sections.title: Diagnostics and logging
sections.blurb: Every developer-facing output is one closed record. Five producers build it, and the sink in force picks the rendering.

rules.title: Every developer-facing output is one closed record
rules.diverges: there is one model behind every diagnostic, so a value's type is never lost the way `print_r` loses it

rules.title: Five producers build the one record
A record names the file, line and member it was produced at, and a `Throwable`'s location is that same datum
rules.diverges: no stack is captured per record, where `getTrace` snapshots the whole stack at construction; the call path is the trace's answer and a record carries only where it was produced

rules.title: Redaction, control bytes, bidi and elision are decided in the record
rules.diverges: a cut, a cycle and a redaction are nodes in the record, so every rendering agrees on them instead of truncating per formatter

rules.title: The sink in force picks the rendering, and no call site may name one
rules.diverges: one member replaces `var_dump`, `print_r`, `var_export` and `json_encode`, and reads correctly in every medium

rules.title: A class cannot change how it is dumped
rules.diverges: no `__debugInfo` and no `__toString` in a dump — a dump shows declared state and never a prettier view of it

rules.title: A dump goes to the log, and reaches a response body only in development
rules.diverges: a forgotten dump writes a log line; the spelling that puts it in a production response does not exist

rules.title: One write path, and the engine floor is its other caller
Five levels, and the mapping to syslog is fixed
rules.diverges: five levels rather than PSR-3's eight, because nobody has a rule for choosing `notice` over `info`

rules.title: A record's fields are named and typed, not a stringly bag
A repeat is bounded at the sink that suffers from it: a disk-bounded target coalesces before the write, and an indexed one groups at read time

sections.title: Ambiguous input is refused
sections.blurb: Where two readings of the same bytes are possible, Novis refuses the whole message rather than repairing it.

rules.title: Ambiguous input is refused whole, never repaired
rules.diverges: nothing is normalised, unfolded, mangled or truncated into an interpretation

rules.title: The closed list of what makes an HTTP message ambiguous
rules.diverges: the outbound half is held to the same list, with no per-call opt-out

rules.title: A cookie name is bytes, and a prefix is enforced once
rules.diverges: no `.`-and-space mangling of cookie names, and `__Host-`/`__Secure-` are enforced by the runtime rather than by every read site

rules.title: A multipart body is capped by part count, not only by size
A path component that does not spell what it resolves to is refused, on every platform
rules.diverges: Windows device names, trailing dots and 8.3 short names are refused on Linux and macOS too

sections.title: What the toolchain is
sections.blurb: No REPL, reflection and parsing built in, and the two claims the project will not make against Python.

rules.title: A file whose first two bytes are `#!` starts in code mode, and its first line is trivia
rules.diverges: a `#!` first line is stripped by PHP but the file still needs `<?php` on line 2; here the shebang itself opens code mode, and a `<?nvs` after it is E0009

rules.title: There is no REPL and none is planned; `nvs run`, `nvs test` and `Core\Debug::dump` are the answer
rules.diverges: there is no `php -a`; the loop an interactive shell serves is `nvs run` over a cached artifact and `nvs test`

rules.title: Reflection and source parsing are built into `Core`, and `Core\Ast` is the compiler's own parser
rules.diverges: `Core\Ast` is built in where PHP needs `nikic/php-parser` or the PECL `ast` extension, and there is no `setAccessible(true)`

rules.title: Against Python, Novis claims the tool that gets handed over; "faster than Python" and "replaces Python" are forbidden

sections.title: The terminal and command-line programs
sections.blurb: Every `echo` has a sink, every control byte is neutralized, styling is a value, and a command table is built while compiling.

rules.title: Every execution context binds `echo` to a sink, and the default sink is the terminal
rules.diverges: `echo` in a scheduled script, a job worker or a test neutralizes control bytes rather than writing raw, and only an HTTP request makes it HTML

rules.title: Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty
rules.diverges: `echo "\e[31m"` prints `␛[31m` rather than turning the text red, on a pipe and a terminal alike; colour is `Core\Cli\Text`

rules.title: `Cli\Text` is the terminal's one raw path, and both of its constructors neutralize their input
An `ESC` in a source literal is a compile error that names `Core\Cli\Text`
rules.diverges: a hand-rolled `"\e[1m"` literal fails the build instead of styling the output

rules.title: Styling is a value type — `Cli\Style` and `Cli\Color` — and never a fifth grammar
rules.diverges: there is no escape string and no `<red>…</red>` markup; a style is `Cli\Style::of({...})` over `Cli\Color` values

rules.title: The terminal profile resolves once per process, and a stream that is not a terminal gets no styling
rules.diverges: `posix_isatty`, `NO_COLOR` handling and `tput cols` are one profile read at start-up; a program writes `Cli\Text` and never asks what the terminal supports

rules.title: `Cli::displayWidth` measures the string the sink will write, in grapheme-cluster columns
rules.diverges: `mb_strwidth` counts code points and sees an escape sequence as zero columns; `displayWidth` counts the substituted string, so a control byte costs one column

rules.title: There is no raw handle onto standard output or standard error, and no cursor, clipboard or title primitive
rules.diverges: `STDOUT`, `STDERR`, `php://stdout` and `fwrite(STDOUT, …)` have no counterpart; byte-exact output names a file, and standard input is `Core\IO::stdin()` alone

rules.title: The tty belongs to the main task of a CLI program, so a `Core\Cli` member throws in a request and in a spawned isolate
rules.diverges: a request handler cannot reach the terminal at all, where PHP-FPM's `STDOUT` quietly lands in the server log

rules.title: In-place output is a scoped live region the runtime paints, never a cursor primitive
rules.diverges: there is no `\r`-and-overwrite progress bar and no cursor movement; `Cli::live` and `Cli::progress` hand the body a handle and paint nothing at all on a pipe

rules.title: A prompt is a `Core\Cli` member that reads the controlling terminal, and `secret` originates a `secret`
rules.diverges: `readline()` reads standard input; `Cli::ask` reads the controlling terminal, so a piped program can still ask a question

rules.title: A prompt never blocks: no terminal or no answer in five minutes takes the `default` or throws `Cli\NotInteractive`
rules.diverges: `readline()` in CI hangs until the pipeline kills it; here it throws, and no `timeout` option lengthens the wait

rules.title: Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region are restored on a throw, a fatal, a panic and a signal
rules.diverges: a script that dies mid-prompt does not leave the shell in raw mode; restoration is the runtime's obligation rather than a `finally` the author remembers

rules.title: `#[Command]` builds the command table while compiling, and a duplicate name or an unbindable option fails the build
rules.diverges: `getopt()` and hand-parsed `$argv` become a table built while compiling; a duplicate command, two options sharing a spelling, or an `#[Option]` on a type no text converts into is a compile error rather than a run-time surprise

rules.title: A command parameter is a positional argument unless it carries `#[Option]`, and its type converts and launders the word
rules.diverges: an argument arrives as the parameter's declared type, `uint` unqualified and `string` `tainted`, instead of every option being a string in an array

rules.title: `Core\Command::run` dispatches to the handler the first word names, and help and completions are generated from the table
rules.diverges: nobody writes a usage block or a completion script; `--help` and `bash`/`zsh`/`fish`/`pwsh` completions are read off the compiled table

sections.title: The formatter
sections.blurb: One canonical style, no configuration, no reflowing of what you wrote — and a fixed point over the input bytes.

rules.title: `nvs fmt` has one style, takes no configuration, and its output is a pure function of the file it is given
rules.diverges: there is no `.php-cs-fixer.php`, no ruleset and no style flag; every knob php-cs-fixer and PHP_CodeSniffer expose is one fixed answer here

rules.title: The base style is PER: four-space indentation, K&R braces on control structures, Allman braces on declarations, and one canonical modifier order
rules.diverges: PER's modifier order is enforced rather than recommended, and `else if` is always written `elseif`

rules.title: `nvs fmt` never decides where an expression breaks: the author's own line breaks are kept and only what surrounds them is normalized
rules.diverges: php-cs-fixer and Prettier-style tools re-wrap to a column limit; here there is no line-length rule at all, soft or hard

rules.title: A string literal is rewritten to single quotes unless it interpolates or contains a single quote, and heredoc bodies and comments are never touched
A comma-separated list that spans more than one line gets a trailing comma, and a list on one line never does
rules.diverges: php-cs-fixer's `trailing_comma_in_multiline` is a choice; here it is the only layout

rules.title: Consecutive `use` declarations are sorted by full path, ascending and case-sensitive, with no blank line between them
rules.diverges: there is no grouped `use A\{B, C};` form to order, because Novis's `use` names exactly one path

rules.title: Every construct PER never saw — qualifiers, `lateinit`, `fn` closures, `match`, object literals, shape types, enum cases, markup literals, a `?>` on its own line — has exactly one layout
`nvs fmt` lower-cases a mis-cased reserved spelling only where that spelling has no other legal meaning — a duration unit and the open tag, never a keyword or an identifier
rules.diverges: PHP's case-insensitive keywords are not normalized; `IF` is a legal class name and fixing an identifier's case is a rename, not a layout

rules.title: `nvs fmt` never inserts a visibility keyword; `nvs convert` inserts `public` as an E-tier rewrite
rules.diverges: php-cs-fixer's `visibility_required` fixer writes the missing `public`; the formatter here never changes meaning, and the insertion happens only in `nvs convert`

rules.title: `nvs fmt` never reorders class members, because declaration order is observable in what a program prints and sends
rules.diverges: php-cs-fixer's `ordered_class_elements` has no counterpart; a member's position is kept

rules.title: `nvs fmt` is a fixed point over the input bytes: byte-stable on every machine, and deliberately not source-independent
`nvs fmt` is a separate opt-in tool: no compiler command runs it, an unformatted file is never a diagnostic, and an editor composes it with quick fixes in the client
rules.diverges: no `php -l`-style check ever holds a stylistic opinion, and formatting never lands in the same report as an error

rules.title: `nvs fmt` rewrites in place; `--check` writes nothing and exits non-zero naming every file that would change; `--diff` prints the diff instead
rules.diverges: `php-cs-fixer fix --dry-run` is the habit; the flag is `--check` and its exit status is the whole contract

sections.title: Doc comments and `nvs meta`
sections.blurb: A doc comment is exactly `///`, and one JSON document is the machine-readable source every renderer consumes.

rules.title: A doc comment is exactly `///`; `////` and longer runs are ordinary comments, and `#` never is one
rules.diverges: there is no `/** */` docblock; the PHPDoc shape is an ordinary comment nothing reads

rules.title: A `///` run attaches to the declaration below it across no blank line, and a doc comment attached to nothing is a diagnostic
A doc comment is Markdown plus `@see` and `@example`, each of which must resolve, and any other `@tag` is a diagnostic
rules.diverges: there is no `@param`, `@return`, `@throws`, `@var` or `@deprecated`; what PHPDoc tags carried is the signature, an attribute or a declared capability

rules.title: Nothing requires a doc comment by default; `nvs check --strict-docs` reports a public member without one, and no autofix can satisfy it
rules.diverges: an IDE cannot answer the check with a generated docblock, because there is no tag to generate

rules.title: `nvs doc <entry>` writes one Markdown page per class from the JSON and has no source of truth of its own
rules.diverges: the renderer ships inside the binary rather than as a phpDocumentor-style tool a project installs

rules.title: `nvs meta --json` is the one machine-readable source of documentation, every renderer consumes it, and no renderer is authoritative for content
rules.diverges: phpDocumentor re-derives documentation from source at every run; here nothing does, and the renderers share one JSON

rules.title: `nvs meta --json` prints the whole `Core` registry as one JSON document, and a field with nothing written is an absent key rather than an empty one
rules.diverges: there is no `php --rf`, no reflection dump and no phpDocumentor pass over the standard library; one command from the binary is the reference's only input

rules.title: `nvs meta --json <entry>` emits that program's own declarations beside the `Core` registry, in the registry's own shape
`nvs agent` answers a coding agent from the registry and the embedded reference chapters in four commands, and the check loop is part of the surface
`nvs agent index` prints one derived line per registered member, carrying its signature and the capability it is gated on, and one per chapter heading
`nvs agent index` carries one derived line per configuration key, command, flag and diagnostic code, and `find` reaches each by the name a user types
Every diagnostic code carries a plain card that `nvs agent show` prints, and a terminal rendering names that command once
The primer is generated, and every refusal it states and every example it shows is proven against the compiler that ships with it
`nvs agent init` writes one pointer per harness, and no adapter ever states a language fact

sections.title: Converting PHP
sections.blurb: One rule table read through two modes, every branch carrying a tier, and not one input byte dropped on the floor.

rules.title: The PHP front end is `php-rs-parser`, pinned, reached only through `nvs_convert::php`, and never linked into the server
rules.diverges: no PHP binary is needed to convert, and the source is read at one declared dialect between 7.4 and 8.6 rather than under whichever PHP is installed

rules.title: `nvs convert` is one rule table read through two modes, and every branch carries a tier
rules.diverges: a Rector run rewrites in one best-effort pass; here every rewrite is proven, annotated or commented out, and the default output is a worklist that does not run

rules.title: Names, constructs and semantic deltas each have one home, and the converter copies none of them
A tier-E rewrite names a differential case against the PHP oracle, or it is not E
`nvs convert` is a pure function of its input bytes, mode, dialect, table digest and flags
rules.diverges: a Rector run iterates to a fixpoint and its output depends on the installed PHP; every pass here runs once, in a fixed order, and no PHP binary is consulted

rules.title: Every non-trivia input byte leaves the converter as code or as comment, and output is re-parsed before it is written
A converted site is annotated `TODO(convert:<id>)`, and `--check` publishes the tier counts as TOML
The converter never runs its input, never converts `vendor/` by default, never invents a binding and never claims compatibility
rules.diverges: no autoloader, bootstrap or `composer install` runs, and a Composer dependency is reported against the package registry rather than ported

sections.title: Benchmarks, telemetry and the update check
sections.blurb: Two independent opt-ins, both off by default, a closed set of counters, and a process serving traffic that never uploads.

rules.title: The benchmark engine list is data, `total` is the CLI headline, and a missing engine never turns a build red
Usage telemetry and the update check are two independent opt-ins, both off by default, and neither ever implies the other
rules.diverges: PHP advertises itself through `X-Powered-By` and measures nothing; here nothing leaves the machine unless the operator switched it on

rules.title: A counter is `invocation.<subcommand>` from the compiled-in command table or `invocation.unknown`, and nothing derived from traffic is ever counted
`nvs telemetry show` prints the exact payload the next upload would send, and the schema, the endpoint contracts and the aggregated data are all published
An upload carries only the previous finished week, rides a short-lived user-initiated command at most weekly, and a process that has bound a socket never uploads
rules.diverges: there is no daemon, no timer and no background process; a server under load makes zero outbound telemetry connections

rules.title: An upload gets three seconds, is abandoned with its counters kept when that expires, says so, and never changes the carrying command's exit status
`nvs update-check` always reports the telemetry switch, the local and latest versions, and with telemetry on its upload history; `--json` is stable and the exit status is always 0

sections.title: The repository's own tools
sections.blurb: One Bun program, one JSON record per fact under `data/`, and generated files that are committed and never edited.

rules.title: The repository's tools are one Bun + TypeScript program, `bun nv`, and `smol-toml` is its only runtime dependency
A fact a repository tool reads is one JSON record under `data/`, its type declared once and its text written by one writer
A file rendered from the records is committed, marked generated and never edited, and a conflict in one is resolved by rendering it again
The chain record names the live goal, and a goal's floor is a view over every walked goal's checks, with the permanent suite's tests graduated
A check runs only when the change reaches what its green runs were observed to use, and the pipeline runs and records on the one `covws` debug build

sections.title: The resilient parse
sections.blurb: One grammar, one tree. The parser always returns something, a node it invented says so, and the file is reproducible byte for byte.

rules.title: The resilient parse is the one grammar's AST plus a trivia layer and an offset index, never a second tree
rules.diverges: a PHP editor — PhpStorm, Intelephense — carries a parser of its own beside `php`; here the editor parses with the compiler's one grammar, so what the editor accepts and what `nvs check` accepts cannot drift

rules.title: Every token and every trivium, concatenated in offset order, reproduce the file byte for byte
A node the parser invented says so — `MemberName::Missing` and a spanned `ExprKind::Error` — and an empty span is never the signal
The parser always returns a tree, a node it invented says so, and an offset maps to the innermost node even inside a malformed region
rules.diverges: an editor over PHP goes dark below the first syntax error until it is fixed; here completion and hover keep working on the well-formed code around it

rules.title: Position encoding is negotiated, every offset conversion lives in `nvs-diagnostics`, and a document's bytes are never normalised
`SyntaxIndex.at(offset)` answers the innermost node and its ancestors, and is rebuilt per analysis
A full re-analysis of a ~1,000-line document stays under a named bound, and the guard is a test rather than an assumption
`nvs ast --json` has a frozen node schema, is resilient by default, and its only type-dependent field is a `secret` literal's placeholder

sections.title: The language server
sections.blurb: Synchronous, one analysis thread, a closed request set, and diagnostics that stop at the first phase that failed.

rules.title: `nvs-lsp` and `editors/vscode` are one crate and one package that grow in place; no prototype is built to be discarded
`nvs-lsp` is synchronous on `lsp-server` and `lsp-types` — a reader thread, a writer thread, one analysis thread, and no async runtime
Each open document is analysed as its own entry point, with open buffers overlaid on disk, and diagnostics are published only for open documents
A file a program autoloads or requires is analysed through that program's `autoload` map, behind its own declarations and without reporting anything for the borrowed ones

A `Core` class, enum, interface or compiler attribute is declared in a generated stub file the server writes once per version, which is what a jump to a `Core` name opens, and which is read-only and never diagnosed
rules.diverges: PhpStorm ships a hand-maintained stub tree for PHP's built-ins; here the stubs are generated from the registry the runtime dispatches on, so a stub cannot say what the binary does not do

rules.title: M4B answers nine standard requests and exactly one of Novis's own, M10 adds eight more on the same test, and that test keeps the list from growing
The first `nvs lsp` answers six requests and two code actions, and nothing else until the workspace index exists
The VS Code client goes as deep as the editor allows, and each feature waits for the language or runtime piece it needs rather than shipping as a stub
A file with a lexer or parser diagnostic publishes those and its declaration diagnostics, and suppresses its own resolution and type diagnostics
rules.diverges: a PHP editor's diagnostics come from one pass with no phase to gate, so a mid-statement typo shows every consequence it cascades into

rules.title: `nvs check --json` writes the same diagnostic records the terminal renderer prints, as one `schemaVersion: 1` document
The symbol index covers every file under the workspace folder by default, and `"open"` narrows it to the open documents and their require graph

sections.title: Code actions and quick fixes
sections.blurb: An action may only write text the compiler already determined — never a choice, never an alias, never a guess.

rules.title: A code action ships only where its replacement text is already in a diagnostic's suggestions — two at M4B, and no other

An inspection is a code action backed by a diagnostic the checker emits, runs on the resilient tree, and is off by default under `source.fixAll.nvs` so it composes with format-on-save while `nvs fmt` stays layout-only
rules.diverges: there is no inspection profile to tune; a fix exists only where a diagnostic already carries its replacement text, and running fixes on save is `editor.codeActionsOnSave`, never part of the formatter

rules.title: An unqualified name that resolves to nothing carries one `use` line per type it could have meant, and the editor offers each as a quick fix
A type name pasted from one file into another brings the `use` line that resolves it, read at copy time from the file it came from
A code action that writes may write only text the type system has already fully determined, and never makes a choice
rules.diverges: implement-missing-members copies real signatures instead of guessing at them, and there is no getter/setter generator because property hooks make the pair pointless

rules.title: Rename, organize-imports and auto-import never write a `use` alias: an import inserts the fully-qualified name, and organize-imports only reorders and removes
rules.diverges: PhpStorm's auto-import may add `use Foo as Bar` to dodge a clash; here an alias is not a spelling the language has, so the editor cannot write one

rules.title: One editor action rewrites an `array<mixed>` annotation to the type of the array literal that initializes it, and rewrites nothing else
rules.diverges: the language never infers an array's type from its literal; the narrowing is an editor edit a person reads in a diff and approves

rules.title: The synthesized element type is the canonical union of the elements' base types, recursed through nested literals and bounded at depth 32
The narrowing action answers from a literal in the same file, or it is not offered: no literal, a `mixed` element, or a no-op each hides it
rules.diverges: a value decoded from input stays `array<mixed>` on purpose and gets no offer, where a PHP editor would happily type it from one observed payload

rules.title: The synthesis is one function in `nvs-types`, called only where `var` types a bare array literal, and a union it finds is never attached to a binding
The narrowing action is never registered under `source.fixAll.nvs` and never chases the call sites it affects, because it breaks writes it cannot see

sections.title: Highlighting, completion and references
sections.blurb: Two highlighting layers that ship names and no colours, and completion that offers only what the compiler already derived.

rules.title: Syntax highlighting is a TextMate grammar and a semantic-token provider, each with its own test, and each must cover what makes Novis not PHP
rules.diverges: type annotations sit where PHP has none — parameters, returns, properties, `foreach` bindings, typed locals, inline shapes — so a borrowed PHP grammar mis-colours the largest part of a Novis file

rules.title: Nothing Novis rejects is coloured as though it were valid
rules.diverges: a PHP grammar colours `===`, `(int)$x` and `if (...): endif;` as syntax; here they render as body text so the editor never confirms what the compiler refuses

rules.title: Semantic tokens use LSP's standard types plus two modifiers of Novis's own, `tainted` and `secret`, and the client's legend must equal the server's
rules.diverges: no PHP tool shows a value's taint at its use sites; here `tainted` and `secret` travel as token modifiers to every use, not only the declaration

rules.title: Both layers ship standard names and no colours: every scope is on the TextMate allowlist, every token type is in LSP's legend, and the extension overrides no theme
Find-references, occurrence highlight, CodeLens, type hierarchy and unused-member dimming are five queries against one workspace index
The editor completes a value only where the compiler already derives it for another reason or a completion file lists it, never from a framework's conventions, an annotation dialect or the network
rules.diverges: framework-aware IntelliSense built from convention scans and annotation dialects has no counterpart; a route name or a directive completes from the table the compiler built, a value from outside the program completes from the JSON files in a `.novis/completion/` folder, which do the job of PhpStorm's `.phpstorm.meta.php`, and an ORM column or a view name has nothing to complete from because Novis has neither

rules.title: A JSON file under a `.novis/completion` folder offers values at the string parameters it names, changes only the string the cursor is in, and is read and never run
rules.diverges: PhpStorm's `.phpstorm.meta.php` is one PHP file it parses for the same purpose; a completion file is JSON, any number of them may sit in any `.novis/completion/` folder, and any program may write one

rules.title: A bare name is offered every type the registry and the workspace index hold, by short name, and accepting one that needs an import writes its `use` line

A trigger character opens a list only where it finished `->`, `::`, `\`, `$` or `<?`, or opened or extended a `require` or `autoload` literal, the string of `as class<T>` or a string argument at a path or class-name parameter, and `$`, a lone `:` and `<?` each narrow what is offered
Accepting a type writes `Name::` inside an expression and `Name()` after `new`, and the name alone wherever a type or a statement may start
Accepting a method writes `name()` with the cursor inside where it takes a parameter, and a property, constant, case or alias writes the name alone
A completion row shows a member's signature after its name and its type at the right, a type its namespace, and the card is read on resolve for one item
A reserved word is offered only where the token before it and the nodes around it let the compiler accept it
A PHP-name completion item takes one of four shapes, and three of them insert nothing
rules.diverges: typing a PHP built-in's name offers an item that may say dropped, waiting on a milestone or undecided and type nothing, rather than inserting the PHP call

rules.title: An inline-HTML region gets the editor's own HTML, CSS and JavaScript services on boundaries the server reports, and the editor's HTML formatter after `nvs fmt`, indented from the Novis code around it
rules.diverges: the markup half of a file gets Emmet, tag closing, the colour picker and the HTML formatter as in a PHP editor, but each markup chunk is indented from the `?>` that opened it — the Novis block's depth — rather than from the markup's own nesting alone

sections.title: Testing the editor
sections.blurb: An LSP answer is frozen as a case file with a cursor, a request and its exact rendering — and coverage is inferred, not declared.

rules.title: `.nvst` and `.lspt` get a grammar of their own, with Novis embedded in `--FILE--` and PHP in `--ORACLE--`
An LSP answer is frozen as a `.lspt` case — a document, a `<|>` cursor, a request and its rendering — run by `nvs lsp-test` printing `N passed, M failed`
`--REQUEST--` is one line whose argument set is closed per request, and an unknown request or argument fails the case
`--EXPECT--` is exact and frozen, and every response is rendered by `nvs_lsp::render` so no case invents a spelling
`.lspt` coverage is inferred from the node the cursor resolved to, never declared, and `every_request_answers_every_construct` names each empty cell
Both tiers run on every acceptance sweep: the headless suites with no editor, and the extension-host run in a pinned build with a throwaway profile

sections.title: One server, thin clients
sections.blurb: Language smarts and formatting have one implementation each. An editor client holds none of either.

rules.title: Language smarts and formatting of Novis have one implementation each, `nvs-lsp` and `nvs-fmt`, and an editor client holds none of either
rules.diverges: PhpStorm's PHP support is a native PSI plugin with its own formatter and refactorings, whereas its Novis plugin is a bridge to the same server VS Code drives, so nothing about `.nvs` is decided in the editor

rules.title: An editor client lives under `editors/<editor>`, outside the Cargo workspace, and is created when its milestone starts rather than scaffolded ahead of it
The VS Code extension is a `vscode-languageclient` shell: it registers `.nvs`, colours from a TextMate grammar until the server answers, and routes everything else to `nvs lsp` and `nvs fmt`
`.nvs` is registered as its own language in every editor, activates nothing on `.php`, and is never handed to a PHP plugin
rules.diverges: a `.nvs` file is not a PHP file to the editor, so Intelephense and PhpStorm's bundled PHP support never open it and none of their settings reach it

rules.title: The extension activates on `.nvs` and never claims `.php`
rules.diverges: opening a `.php` file gets the PHP extension already installed, not Novis, even though `nvs-syntax` could parse it

rules.title: `language-configuration.json` carries comments, pairs, indentation, folding and a `wordPattern` that includes `$`
rules.diverges: double-clicking `$total` selects `$total`; a configuration borrowed from a PHP extension selects `total` and puts every rename-adjacent interaction off by one character

rules.title: Writing a `///` run is the editor's job: `onEnterRules` continues one, a paste provider prefixes one, and neither contributes a name
rules.diverges: a PHP editor continues a `/** */` docblock and autocompletes tags into it; here the continuation is a `///` run and there is no tag to complete

rules.title: A setting name and a command id are public API: the roster is frozen, and anything later is added, never renamed

sections.title: Inside the VS Code extension
sections.blurb: What the extension contributes, why it builds no UI the editor already has, and where its clients live in the tree.

rules.title: `nvs run` and `nvs test` are Tasks with a `problemMatcher` over the renderer's own format, so a diagnostic is a Problems-panel entry
The extension declares itself a workspace extension, because `nvs lsp` must be the binary next to the code
The extension is `novis-lang.nvs`, language `nvs`, `extensionKind: ["workspace"]`, built as a `.vsix` and published nowhere
The extension ships no `nvs` binary: a missing one is a guided install the user starts, verified against the release's own `SHA256SUMS`

Coverage, server health, profiles and the debugger reach the editor through its own APIs and open formats — `FileCoverage`, `LanguageStatusItem`, DAP's UI, speedscope — and the extension builds none of them
rules.diverges: Xdebug's profiler writes cachegrind for KCachegrind or PhpStorm's own viewer; a Novis profile is speedscope JSON and opens in speedscope.app or an embedded view of it

rules.title: The Test Explorer is `nvs test --list` and `nvs test --format=json` projected: the client matches records to items and derives nothing
The AST panel renders `nvs ast --json` for the active file, on the resilient tree by default, and never runs `Core\Ast`
`package-lock.json` is committed; `node_modules/`, `out/`, `.vscode-test/` and `*.vsix` are ignored

sections.title: PhpStorm and the debugger
sections.blurb: The same server behind another editor, and a debug adapter that is complete before any debugger UI exists.

rules.title: PhpStorm drives the same `nvs lsp` and `nvs fmt` through JetBrains' LSP client, and builds no PSI tree, native refactoring or debugger UI until a later decision says so
rules.diverges: Reformat Code runs `nvs fmt` with no PhpStorm Code Style page behind it, and PSI-level refactoring, structural search and the native debugger are absent for `.nvs`

rules.title: `nvs dap` is complete without any editor's debugger UI; VS Code's wiring is a descriptor factory and a `launch.json` schema, and PhpStorm's stays deferred
rules.diverges: there is no Xdebug-style listener to configure in the editor; the editor points its own debugger UI at `nvs dap` and renders what the adapter reports

rules.title: The debugger UI is only as deep as the capabilities `nvs dap` reports, so the adapter's capability list is the debugger's scope
rules.diverges: break-on-uncaught and break-on-thrown are two exception filters rather than PHP's five categories, and a spawned isolate appears as a thread rather than as a second session

sections.title: Security in the editor
sections.blurb: What security means once a file is open rather than running: the process on the wire, the binary the client will trust, and a secret concealed on screen. None of it is a language guarantee.

rules.title: Nothing but the protocol writes to the server's stdout; logging goes to stderr and `window/logMessage`
On a version mismatch at `initialize` the client says so in the status item and does not start
Every process the extension starts runs from a verified copy of the binary that is never older than the build on disk, so the file the user named is never held
The extension holds no language logic, and its `package.json` dependencies are checked against an allowlist by its own tests
The editor conceals a `secret` value by default, and the ranges come from the language server rather than a client guess
Only the bytes are concealed — a literal token or an interpolation slot, never an identifier or an annotation
A reveal is per range, window-local, and does not survive the editor closing
What the editor's concealment cannot cover is written down, because a redaction trusted past its reach is worse than none
The redaction request is one server's to answer for both editors, but the drawing is per-editor and PhpStorm has none until its plugin lands
`tainted` ships no default editor decoration, and the marker is opt-in

sections.title: Writing a test
sections.blurb: A test is a method with an attribute, running in its own isolate, asserting on two values of one type.

rules.title: A test is a method marked `#[Test]`, and its table is built while compiling
rules.diverges: there is no test framework to install, no naming convention and no base class; a malformed test is a compile error rather than a case that silently never runs

rules.title: `nvs run` and `nvs build` lower no test, and `nvs check` type-checks every one
rules.diverges: test code is absent from a built artifact by construction, rather than excluded by whatever the deployment happened to copy

rules.title: Every test runs in its own isolate and shares nothing but compiled code with its siblings
rules.diverges: total isolation is the default rather than a per-case escape hatch; a static one test wrote is never visible to the next

rules.title: A test reaches `private` members of classes declared in its own file, and nowhere else
rules.diverges: there is no reflection to reach a private member with, so white-box testing is bought by co-location and by nothing else

rules.title: An assertion names its subject first and compares two values of one type
rules.diverges: the argument order is `(actual, expected)`, the reverse of PHPUnit's, and comparing an `int` against a `string` does not compile

rules.title: A failed assertion is a catchable `Throwable` and a ledger entry the test cannot erase
