rules.diverges: a `catch (Throwable)` around a failing assertion cannot turn a red test green; the runner reads its own ledger rather than the exception state

rules.title: The constructor is the test's setup, and there is no second before-hook
rules.diverges: there is no `setUp`, `setUpBeforeClass` or `tearDownAfterClass`; the constructor is the only one, and every property is assigned before any test body runs

rules.title: `#[After]` is for state that outlives the isolate, and nothing else needs teardown
`#[Fixture]` is built once per class and injected into a test by the type it returns
rules.diverges: shared setup is resolved by declared type while compiling, so an unsatisfiable parameter is a diagnostic rather than a null at run time

rules.title: `#[TestWith]` is matched against the parameters by name and by type, and each row is its own case
rules.diverges: a data provider is a checked attribute payload rather than an `array<array<mixed>>` a method returns, so a row that does not fit the signature is refused where it is written

sections.title: Doubles, determinism and the runner
sections.blurb: Structural doubles, a fixed clock and seed, property tests, inline snapshots — and a runner that refuses to call nothing green.

rules.title: A double is a shape of closures, structurally checked against an interface
rules.diverges: no class is generated and no source is evaluated; a double is a value the checker compares against the interface, and a loose or nice double is not expressible

rules.title: A call to a double is asserted after the exercise, never expected before it
rules.diverges: there is no `expects()`; the method being asserted on is a compile-checked reference, so renaming it breaks the test rather than leaving it passing

rules.title: `at:` and `seed:` fix the clock and the generator of the test's own isolate
rules.diverges: time and randomness are controlled by a declaration on the test rather than by a clock parameter threaded through every time-aware class

rules.title: A task still running when a test returns fails that test
`#[Test(db:)]` opens a transaction on the test's own context and rolls it back
A test request is dispatched in-process through the compiled route table, and its input arrives `tainted`
rules.diverges: an HTTP test needs no socket, no port and no web server; the real route table and the real middleware chain answer it in microseconds

rules.title: One registered answer makes every outbound call in that test come from the table, and an unmatched one throws rather than reaching the network
rules.diverges: there is no way to intercept `curl_exec` short of a wrapper the application was written around or a stub extension; here one registered answer takes the whole test off the network

rules.title: `Core\Test`'s table answers a WebSocket handshake, plays the frames it was given and records what the program sent, and an unmatched socket throws rather than connecting
`#[Property]` derives its generators from the parameters' declared types
A snapshot is a literal in the test body, and the updater rewrites that literal and nothing else
A mutation run asks whether any test would have noticed the code being wrong
A test that asserts nothing fails, a skip states a reason, and a retry is reported flaky rather than green
rules.diverges: a test with no assertion is a failure rather than a risky-marked pass, and a case that only passed on a retry never counts as green

rules.title: One verdict, three renderings, a machine format owns stdout alone, and the JSON one locates every test it reports
`nvs test` writes line coverage as lcov and Clover, from one hit table every context of the run counts into
rules.diverges: there is no coverage driver to install; the probes are already in every compiled unit, and the flags are PHPUnit's `--coverage-clover` with `--coverage-lcov` beside it

sections.title: Feature proofs
sections.blurb: A feature is finished when it has a description, a test from both sides, three examples, a measured figure and an attack against it.

rules.title: `.nvst` proves the language; `#[Test]` is how a program written in Novis tests itself
A directory handed to `nvs test` that holds `.nvs` files is one program requiring every one of them in name order, and a file in it that requires the bootstrap gives it its `autoload` map
One slice writes all of a feature's proofs together
`docs/examples/` is authoritative and the website mirrors it
A hostile case passes when nothing came apart, and a compile diagnostic is never a pass
A feature is finished when its feature proofs exist: a description, a test from both sides, three examples, a measured figure, an attack and its help in the binary
The roster of features is read from the registry and the reference chapters, never kept as a list
An example, an attack and a bench are attributed by path; a test is attributed by a marker
A proof that fails is fixed or recorded as a known gap, and never weakened

sections.title: Coverage, tracing and the debug probes
sections.blurb: One per-request flag word at fixed probe sites, exporting formats existing tooling already reads — never a second compiled tier.

rules.title: Every member of a capability-bearing class declares a capability or declares none, and there is no allowlist
The third-party notice is committed, and a check fails when the lockfile moved without it
`[debug] mode` is the ceiling as well as the default, and writing a trace or a profile is its own capability
Coverage, tracing and profiling are one per-request flag word checked at fixed probe sites, never a second compiled tier
rules.diverges: there is no instrumented build and no extension to load; the probes are compiled into every unit and a bit is flipped on a request already in flight

rules.title: Each probe starts and stops mid-request, and exports what existing tooling already reads
The conformance suite runs with the probes on, and once per optimisation level
`[debug] store` is off by default and can only subtract, so no run mode or log level ever turns debug records on
A debug record reaches the service through a sealed spool file that one writer owns, never over a socket
The ingester owns every write to the index and runs without a browser, and the viewer only ever reads
A malformed line becomes a visible record and an unreadable file is quarantined under a backoff, so ingestion never stops
The viewer renders the correlated request stream and hands every artifact with an existing viewer to it

sections.title: Measuring performance
sections.blurb: Counted semantic work rather than wall-clock, a per-PR guard separate from the historical dashboard, and an append-only history.

rules.title: `#[Bench]` reports counted semantic work, and CI may gate on the counts but never on wall-clock
A per-PR guard and the historical dashboard are separate measurements, and never one
Wall-clock and the PHP ratio ride beside the instruction count as same-host figures only
The performance history is an append-only NDJSON file in the repository
A member's record is four counts that compare on any machine and one clock that compares on its own, re-measured only when its implementing file's code moves
A cross-engine comparison is a `benches/userland/` case with one twin per engine
The historical leg runs under callgrind on Linux or WSL, and nowhere else

sections.title: Continuous integration
sections.blurb: One workflow, three lanes, and one table that decides what a given diff has to run.

rules.title: One workflow holds every job, and three lanes decide which of them a run needs
One Python table decides what a diff runs, and the platform matrix is never one of the gates
A run with no base commit to diff against runs every lane
Miri, the fuzzers and the unsafe audit run nightly and at release, and the fuzz corpus persists
A job a lane defers is skipped by its own `if:`, never filtered out of the workflow
A run on `main` is never cancelled by the next commit

sections.title: Isolates
sections.blurb: Running another script shares nothing but compiled code. Values cross by copy, failure crosses as data, and the budget is the tree.

rules.title: Running another script is an in-process isolate that shares nothing with its parent but compiled code
rules.diverges: there is no subprocess and no `exec('php …')`; a second script runs in this process, under this request's budget and its own arena

rules.title: A value crosses an isolate boundary as one graph copy, and a closure, an alias or a host handle does not cross at all
A request and everything it spawns share one budget, accounted at the tree's root
rules.diverges: a spawned unit of work receives no budget of its own; it spends the one the inbound request already holds

rules.title: A child isolate's failure arrives as data on the result and never unwinds into its parent
An isolate's output is captured by default and carries the parent's sink carrier
An isolate ends by draining its roots through the one release worklist and then sweeping what a cycle held up
An isolate's arena is an ownership root, not an address range
An inbound request is the root isolate of its own tree, and there is one isolate implementation

sections.title: The closed doors
sections.blurb: No FFI, no `eval`, no scheme-dispatching path, no cross-request state. Four doors closed by construction, reopened by nothing.

rules.title: Executing code is its own capability, and the entry path is canonicalised and then prefix-checked
Request, server and session state throws where there is no inbound request, rather than answering empty
rules.diverges: `$_GET` inside an included file is the parent's array; here the accessor throws, because a child is not a request

rules.title: Nothing a request does is observable by another request except through an explicit, capability-gated store
rules.diverges: `shmop`, `sysvshm`, APCu, `putenv`, `setlocale`, `bcscale`, `mb_internal_encoding` and `date_default_timezone_set` have no replacement

rules.title: Four doors are closed by construction, and no configuration reopens any of them
rules.diverges: FFI, stream wrappers, shared memory and `eval` are absent rather than disabled, so no safety claim downstream needs an "unless it is enabled"

rules.title: No userland mechanism loads native code into the process
rules.diverges: there is no `FFI`, no `dl()` and no `com_dotnet`; wrapping a native library is a wasm component instead

rules.title: There is no `eval`, and no `Core` member compiles a string produced at run time
rules.diverges: `eval`, a string-argument `assert` and `create_function` do not exist in any spelling

rules.title: A path is a filesystem path: no member dispatches on a scheme prefix, and nothing may register one
rules.diverges: `phar://`, `php://filter`, `data://` and `http://` are file names that do not exist, not protocols

rules.title: A reflective call faces exactly the visibility check ordinary code at that site would, and there is no `setAccessible`
rules.diverges: `ReflectionProperty::setAccessible(true)` and every equivalent are rejected outright, not merely undocumented

rules.title: Reflection and AST parsing are capability-free, because neither reaches the world outside the process

sections.title: Capabilities and authority
sections.blurb: The check lives inside the function that performs the effect, and authority belongs to the namespace enclosing the code.

rules.title: The capability check lives inside the function that performs the effect, and that door is the only way out of the process
rules.diverges: there is no `open_basedir`, no `disable_functions` and no safe mode; the runtime cannot reach the OS except through a checked door

rules.title: A capability question is a grant and a scope, asked of the request's own configuration snapshot
What each `Core` member needs is declared once in one table, and nothing at run time reads it
Every capability name that exists is on one roster, and a name outside it is refused where it is written
Authority is a property of the namespace enclosing the code, never of the nesting depth or the name being called
The application's grant table is keyed on namespace prefixes, and a capability it names must be on the roster
The longest matching grant key wins, and a subtree is spelled out because it reaches code that does not exist yet
A namespace matching no grant line holds the application's own authority, and a fetch leaves nothing unmatched

sections.title: Scopes, denial and the address policy
sections.blurb: How a path scope is decided, why a denial is catchable, and why the network address policy lives inside the capability itself.

rules.title: A path scope is canonicalise-then-prefix over whole components, and a path that does not exist yet is its deepest existing ancestor
rules.diverges: `..` and a planted symlink cannot leave a granted root, because the comparison is made after resolution and never on the text

rules.title: A denied capability is a catchable `RuntimeError` naming the capability, never a fatal
A capability is required or optional, and only a required one refuses to build
Two layers enforce a capability and only the static one grants; nothing anywhere widens
A member that needs no capability pays nothing, and one that does pays only beside a syscall
A dependency's authority is granted by the application one line at a time, and a declaration grants nothing
Executing a program is deny-by-default under its own capability, and there is no shell to interpolate into
rules.diverges: `shell_exec`, `system`, `passthru` and the backtick operator do not exist; there is an argv array and a grant

rules.title: `net.connect` carries an address policy that denies the private ranges, and an exception is one written IP address
The grant follows what the program is doing rather than the transport: reaching out is `net.connect`, binding is `net.listen`, and neither widens the other
The address policy lives in the capability, so every client obeys it and none of them may hold its own

sections.title: Tainted data and its sinks
sections.blurb: Everything from outside arrives `tainted`, it poisons what it touches, and a sink is any parameter a parser will execute.

rules.title: `tainted` is a compile-time qualifier on `string`, `bytes` and a shape of them, spellable in any declaration and erased before codegen
rules.diverges: untrusted input has a type PHP has no way to spell, and a program that mixes it into a sink does not compile

rules.title: Every accessor that hands a program bytes from outside answers the `tainted` form, and the list of them is enumerable
A tainted operand poisons every operation it takes part in, and only a checked conversion launders for free
A `string` or `bytes` parameter is a sink when its content becomes an instruction a parser executes
A `Core` parameter nobody classified refuses a tainted argument, and refuses to ship at all
Every grammar the library parses is a sink, and none of the four gets a launderer
A regex pattern is a sink with no launderer; the subject is data and may be tainted
An outbound URL or address is a sink, and a tainted one is refused where it is written
A metric label value refuses `tainted`, and there is deliberately no launderer for one
A log field is data, so it takes a tainted value and wants one

sections.title: Laundering
sections.blurb: The only ways out of `tainted`: a member named for the one sink it is safe for, a typed capture, or a written assertion.

rules.title: The only way out of `tainted` is a `Core` member whose contract names the one sink it is safe for
rules.diverges: there is no `sanitize()`, no `clean()` and no `filter_var` catch-all; a value safe for HTML is not safe for a path

rules.title: A launderer answers its sink's carrier when that sink launders on its own and the transform is not idempotent, and a plain type otherwise
rules.diverges: `htmlspecialchars($x)` in a string-building position does not compile, because escaping twice is a corruption the type can refuse

rules.title: Capturing a sink yields that sink's carrier, never a plain `string`
A route capture is laundered by the parameter's own type, and a `string` capture stays tainted
A derived codec adds no qualifier rule, and a `secret` field is refused at the declaration rather than silently omitted
`Core\Taint::assertTrusted` is the one generic way out, and it carries a written reason at the call site
A response body is written by one typed member, and mixing `echo` with one of them does not compile
A pooled database connection is proven clean before it is reused, and a failed reset destroys it

sections.title: Secrets
sections.blurb: A second, independent qualifier. Every sink refuses it, it crosses no boundary, comparing two is constant-time, and no rendering the toolchain prints carries one in the clear.

rules.title: `secret` is a second, independent compile-time qualifier, written before `tainted` and in that order alone
rules.diverges: confidentiality is a type, so a credential reaching a page, a log or an exception message is a compile error

rules.title: Nothing grants `secret` ambiently; it appears where a developer wrote it, and at one member that is its own contract
A `secret` operand poisons its own axis independently of `tainted`, and a checked conversion strips it
Every output sink refuses a `secret` value outright, and no auto-escape or neutralisation bypasses one
rules.diverges: `echo $apiKey`, `var_dump($key)` and a credential interpolated into an exception message are all compile errors

rules.title: A `secret` value is refused at the one graph copy, so it reaches neither `serialize` nor any spawn
Comparing two `secret` values with `==` lowers to a constant-time helper, decided by the compiler
rules.diverges: `$a == $b` over two credentials is not a timing oracle, and no call site has to remember `hash_equals`

rules.title: A `secret` operand is compared but never rendered, and no flag lifts the redaction
No rendering the toolchain itself produces prints a `secret` in the clear, the AST dump included

sections.title: Qualifiers across an extension
sections.blurb: An extension manifest may only tighten. Contagion is the default, and no spelling anywhere removes a qualifier.

rules.title: Everything an extension manifest may declare is a restriction, so a hostile manifest cannot make a calling program less safe
An extension's files and outbound HTTP are the intersection of its entry's grant, its manifest's request and its caller's own grant
rules.diverges: a PHP extension acts with the whole process's authority; a Novis extension holds only what three parties all grant

rules.title: An extension call is an ordinary operation for taint, so contagion is the default and needs no declaration
An extension manifest may declare exactly two things: a parameter that refuses `tainted`, and a return that is always `tainted`
No extension may remove the `tainted` qualifier, in any manifest spelling
A `secret` value is refused at every extension boundary, in either direction
The image component declares no qualifier deviation and requests no capability

sections.title: Protocols, tokens and CSRF
sections.blurb: One TLS client, a closed protocol roster, an algorithm that comes from the key, and CSRF on by default.

rules.title: There is one TLS client in the tree, and a driver reaches it over a generic transport rather than building a second
Verification is relaxed only where a `capabilities.tls` grant names the host and the call asks for it, and no such grant has a `true` spelling
rules.diverges: `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = false` is one line of userland; here the same effect needs the deployment to name the host in a grant and the call to ask for it, and the boot prints every grant that was written

rules.title: A closed roster of application-layer security protocols lives in `Core`, and nothing joins it without meeting the test
Three conditions and one boundary decide what may join the roster, and a flow never does
The algorithm comes from the key and never from the token
rules.diverges: `alg: none` and the RS256-to-HS256 confusion have no code path, because no attacker-supplied string selects a verifier

rules.title: A JWT without an expiry, or past one, fails verification, and no flag disables the check
Verification answers a value or throws, and no member exposes a raw comparison for the caller to get wrong
rules.diverges: no verifier returns a falsy value a loose comparison could read as success

rules.title: A verified signature proves origin, not safety: claims come back `tainted`
`Core\Jwe` speaks compact JWE with `A256GCM` alone, and the static that built the key picks the algorithm
rules.diverges: there is no `zip`, no `jku` and no `x5u`, so a token cannot talk the verifier into a fetch or a decompression

rules.title: A token another party issued verifies against a key found by `kid`, never one that is tried, and its claims come back as a `tainted` shape
rules.diverges: a token with no `kid` cannot be walked against a key set, so verification costs one signature check whatever the sender wrote

rules.title: The server refuses an unsafe verb without a valid CSRF token, and the opt-out is written on the route itself
rules.diverges: a deployment with nothing configured already rejects a forged `POST`

rules.title: The compiler proves a route's access decision was written, never that it was honoured

sections.title: Bidirectional text and password hashes
sections.blurb: A two-counter predicate against direction-flipping source, and a hash surface that writes one algorithm and reads exactly two.

rules.title: A span is rejected when it ends with a directional scope still open, decided by two counters
rules.diverges: a Trojan Source payload does not survive the lexer, and there is no attribute that switches the check off

rules.title: The lexer refuses an unterminated control and the sinks substitute it, and nobody writes a second predicate
Zero-width characters, homoglyphs and the full bidirectional algorithm are deliberately outside the check
`hash` writes Argon2id and nothing else, and no member takes an algorithm argument
rules.diverges: `password_hash($p, PASSWORD_BCRYPT)` has no spelling; the algorithm is not a parameter

rules.title: A stored password hash is read from a roster of exactly two shapes, and the roster grows only by amendment
rules.diverges: `$2x$` is refused rather than emulated, because verifying it means reimplementing `crypt_blowfish`'s overflow

rules.title: `needsRehash` measures weaker rather than different, so every bcrypt hash asks to be rewritten
rules.diverges: PHP compares the stored parameters for difference; this answers whether the stored hash is weaker than what `hash` writes now

rules.title: A stored bcrypt cost above 17 is refused before any work is done
bcrypt's 72-byte truncation is replicated exactly, because the stored row was written under it
A stored value outside the read roster throws, and the message never quotes the bytes
rules.diverges: `password_verify` answers `false` for a column it cannot read; this throws, so a wrong column wakes an operator

sections.title: Tasks
sections.blurb: Every task is a child of the one that started it. Control never leaves a group with a child still running.

rules.title: Concurrency is the `Core\Task` roster over the runtime's own single scheduler
rules.diverges: a PHP request has no concurrency to express at all, and the nearest equivalents — `curl_multi_*`, `pcntl_fork`, an extension's own event loop — have no counterpart here

rules.title: Every task is a child of the task that started it, shares that request's accounting, and dies with it
rules.diverges: PHP has no task, so it has no orphan either; here an unparented task is impossible rather than discouraged

rules.title: A child spawned `on: "worker"` is started on another core, copies at every node in both directions, and is still its parent's child
rules.diverges: PHP places nothing — a request is one core's worth of work, and its nearest equivalent is another process, which shares not even the compiled code

rules.title: `Core\Task::all` answers a shape with the argument's own field names, each field keeping its own type
rules.diverges: there is no PHP construct that runs several calls at once and hands back their results already typed

rules.title: An `all` field answers its own callable's declared return type, and a callable declaring none answers `mixed`
`Core\Task::map` answers an array of the callback's own return type, in the input's keys and order
rules.diverges: `array_map` runs sequentially; this one runs the callback concurrently and still answers in the input's order

rules.title: `{limit, deadline}` is the whole of what bounds a group, and there is no `timeout` member and no `race`
rules.diverges: a wait is bounded by an option on the call rather than by `set_time_limit`, `default_socket_timeout` or an ini setting read from somewhere else

rules.title: Control never leaves `all` or `map` with a child still running
rules.diverges: a PHP script that starts something in the background has no construct that waits for it, so nothing there guarantees this

rules.title: A cancelled task runs no `catch`, no cleanup and no handler, and cancellation is not a `Throwable`
rules.diverges: the `finally`-shaped cleanup a PHP developer would reach for does not run, and there is nothing to catch

rules.title: A deadline bounds when cancellation is asked for, not when the call returns

sections.title: Deferred work and cross-request state
sections.blurb: Work that outlives the response but not the request, and the only way a value outlives the request that made it.

rules.title: `Core\Task::afterResponse` runs after the request's own frame returns, still charged to the request tree
rules.diverges: `fastcgi_finish_request` keeps the whole worker busy with no accounting, no cap and no deadline; this keeps the tree, and the tree is still bounded

rules.title: Only the request's own task may defer work, and deferred work may not defer more
Deferred work may read the request but not write the response, and its uncaught throw reaches the log alone
rules.diverges: output written after `fastcgi_finish_request` is silently discarded; here it is refused, at compile time where the call is statically visible

rules.title: `[deferred]` carries two bounds: a `System` `max_concurrent` and a `Runtime` `deadline`
Past `[deferred] max_concurrent`, `afterResponse` throws at the call site rather than queueing
rules.diverges: there is no queue in front of this and no silent backlog; overload is reported to the request that caused it

rules.title: A value outlives the request that made it only by being put into a named store
rules.diverges: APCu, `shmop`, `sysvshm`, `sysvsem` and `sysvmsg` are gone, and there is no ambient place a value can be left for the next request to find

rules.title: `Core\Cache::process()` is one store per serving process, coherent across its cores and gone when it ends
rules.diverges: APCu's segment is shared between every worker of an FPM pool and outlives any one of them; this tier is one process's own memory and goes when that process does

rules.title: The cache boundary is a copy in and a copy out, so nothing a program can reach is read-modify-write
rules.diverges: `apcu_add`, `apcu_cas` and `apcu_inc` have no counterpart, so a lock or a counter is not built on the cache at all

rules.title: A value is copied into the cache and copied back out, by the same graph copy the isolate boundary uses
rules.diverges: APCu's serialize-on-store is a wire format with its own type losses; this is the language's own copy, and it refuses what may not cross rather than mangling it

rules.title: The local tier's memory is charged to the core, capped in `nvs.toml`, and the cap evicts rather than failing a write
rules.diverges: `apc.shm_size` exhaustion makes a store fail; here the cap forgets an older entry and the write succeeds

rules.title: A cross-request store's bytes go on a balance of their own, and no request is charged or credited for them
Anything a program relies on the value of goes to the shared tier, and a weaker tier is not offered for it
rules.diverges: an APCu-backed session, lock or rate limit does not port: the local tier is not among the backends, so the miswiring is a configuration error rather than a race

rules.title: A secret reaches a cache only as ciphertext, through `putSecret` and `getSecret` and a key ring
rules.diverges: there is no counterpart at all: PHP has no confidential type, so a token in APCu or memcached is plaintext by construction

rules.title: On a miss, one caller per process runs `fill` while the others wait, and a failure is never shared
rules.diverges: nothing in PHP coordinates a miss between workers, so a cold key is one fetch per worker and a cached failure is the usual workaround

sections.title: Persistent connections
sections.blurb: A WebSocket or an SSE stream is a root isolate with a loop in it, upgraded from a request that then ends.

rules.title: A persistent connection is a root isolate, and the request that upgraded it ends
rules.diverges: there is nothing a PHP process can hold across requests, so a connection has no counterpart at all — and it is a root rather than a request that never ends

rules.title: An upgrade names compiled code — a file or a static method — and never a closure
rules.diverges: there is no handler object and no closure to hand a socket to; the entry is named at the call site the way a spawned script names one, and its arguments are copied rather than shared

rules.title: An upgrade's `args`, `limits`, `grants` and `on` are a spawned script's options as ordinary named arguments
Inside a connection, code is an ordinary loop, and `receive()` answering `null` is what ends it
rules.diverges: there is no `onMessage` callback and no event registration — suspension has no colour, so a blocking-shaped `while` is the whole program

rules.title: `receive()` is the one wait, and it answers the peer or a subscribed topic, whichever arrives first
What a peer sent arrives `tainted`, and `Core\Validate` is the only way to launder it
rules.diverges: a frame is untrusted by type rather than by convention, so it reaches no sink until it has been validated

rules.title: A stream that ends with its response is a streaming response; one that outlives it is a connection isolate
rules.diverges: the choice is made by lifetime rather than by protocol, and there is no `flush`-in-a-loop shape that keeps a request alive

rules.title: `Core\Socket` and `Core\Sse` are two hand-overs onto one isolate, and each reports the one it is missing
Every bound on an open connection is finite with nothing configured
rules.diverges: there is no unbounded wait to configure your way into: an idle, a lifetime and a send timeout all apply before any configuration is written

rules.title: An open connection runs to completion on the code it started with, and an edit reaches only the next one
rules.diverges: a deploy does not break what is open — there is no per-request re-read of a file a live connection is standing in

rules.title: A shutdown or a reload closes a connection with a defined code after a drain, never with a reset

sections.title: The job queue
sections.blurb: Enqueue commits with your own write. Four members, at-least-once delivery, finite attempts, and a dead letter that is kept.

rules.title: A `push` on the queue's connection commits with the write that caused it, or neither happens
rules.diverges: a queued job and the database write that justified it commit together, where an application on a broker writes an outbox row and relays it afterwards

rules.title: `Core\Queue`'s four request-path members are each asked about a job or about a queue, never about a row number
rules.diverges: the queue is four members of the runtime rather than a framework façade, and what `push` answers is a handle rather than an integer id

rules.title: A `tag` names a group of jobs and a `key` admits one pending job, and they are two columns because they are opposites
A job names a script file, and its payload crosses as a copied value
rules.diverges: a job is a file rather than a class implementing an interface, and nothing about it is a serialized object graph waiting to be reconstructed

rules.title: A job's budget and grants are recorded when it is enqueued, and narrowed from that context rather than widened
rules.diverges: background work carries its own memory, CPU and time budget, and its permissions can only shrink from those of the code that enqueued it

rules.title: A worker claims a job with one statement the database arbitrates, so a fleet needs no lease protocol
rules.diverges: a fleet needs no supervisor, no heartbeat and no coordinator process — the database provides the mutual exclusion

rules.title: A job between attempts is `Pending`, and there is no `Failed` state to ask about
rules.diverges: there is no failed state to poll for — a job waiting out its backoff is indistinguishable from one that has not run yet, and "did it fail" is a question about the dead-letter table

rules.title: Delivery is at-least-once, and idempotency is the job's own obligation
rules.diverges: the guarantee is stated rather than implied, so a job is written to tolerate running twice instead of assuming it will not

rules.title: Attempts are finite, backoff is exponential and jittered, and an exhausted job is kept rather than discarded
rules.diverges: nothing is discarded silently and nothing retries forever — an exhausted job is a row in a dead-letter table rather than a line in a log

rules.title: A job that exceeds its budget is a failed attempt, reported as that and retried like any other
rules.diverges: exhausting memory in background work is a bounded failed attempt rather than a fatal that takes the process with it

sections.title: Running a job
sections.blurb: A job is a root isolate on a recorded budget. Which process runs it is configuration, and there is no pluggable driver.

rules.title: `cancel` answers whether it won the race, and it changes the job's state rather than deleting the row
rules.diverges: cancelling is a race against a worker rather than a command, and the answer says which side won it

rules.title: A queue row is removed by `delete` or `purge`, never while claimed, and never dead-lettered or pending unless the call says so
rules.diverges: removing queued work is two members of the runtime behind a capability, rather than a framework command or a raw delete against a table the runtime owns

rules.title: A job runs as a root isolate, and there is no second execution path
rules.diverges: a job shares nothing with the request that enqueued it — no statics, no session, no superglobals — because it is a fresh isolate rather than the same process continuing

rules.title: Which process runs a job is configuration, and every spelling drives the identical isolate
rules.diverges: workers are the runtime's own and start from configuration — there is no separate daemon or process manager to install beside the server

rules.title: `nvs serve` runs the accept loop, the schedule ticker and the queue's workers in one process, and the drain stops all three
rules.diverges: one process is the whole deployment — there is no process manager, no worker daemon and no cron entry beside it

rules.title: A durable payload refuses `secret`, and a `tainted` value comes back `tainted`
rules.diverges: a credential cannot enter a job payload at all, and taint survives the round trip through the database instead of being laundered by it

rules.title: A `push` on a connection other than the queue's is not transactional, and is counted rather than assumed away
rules.diverges: losing atomicity between a write and its job is a measured deployment fact rather than an unstated one

rules.title: An idle queue worker asks its queue once a second, and a push in the same process wakes it once the job is committed
Queued work is durable, retried and declared by the application; scheduled work is a clock tick and none of those
rules.diverges: cron-style entries and background jobs are two mechanisms with two guarantees, rather than one worker loop doing both

rules.title: There is no broker backend and no pluggable driver, because a driver makes transactional enqueue optional
rules.diverges: there is no Redis, SQS or AMQP backend to choose and nothing to configure between the application and its jobs

sections.title: The scheduler underneath
sections.blurb: Futures, wakers and parking: how a task suspends, what a wake is permission to do, and why a task never migrates cores.

rules.title: A connection is one future, driven to completion by the coroutine that owns it
A waker decides nothing; it is permission to make one more poll happen
One wake permission is installed per drive, and a fresh one is issued only after it fires
A wake from another core queues an id on the task's own core and never migrates it
A wake handle dropped unused wakes its task, unless that task is the one dropping it
A cancellation ends the drive: torn down where it parked, or told once and answered
Where a drive parks is decided once when it starts, and off a core it blocks the thread
A task registers before it suspends, treats a wake as a hint, and leaves the reactor holding nothing when it ends
rules.diverges: a request that waits on I/O suspends one task and hands its core to another, rather than occupying a process until the kernel answers

rules.title: A stream issues the syscall first and parks only on `WouldBlock`, so a warm socket pays nothing
rules.diverges: a read that would block suspends the task rather than the process, and a socket with bytes already buffered costs one ordinary syscall

rules.title: The reactor reports readiness on every platform, Windows included, so a stream is written once
rules.diverges: there is no event loop to install and no extension to pick — readiness is the runtime's own and behaves the same on all three platforms

rules.title: A parking stream is a plain `Read` and `Write`, so nothing up the call chain is coloured
rules.diverges: there is no `await` and no second spelling of any member that touches I/O — a helper reads a socket with the call it would use on a blocking one

rules.title: A task's stack is 1 MiB of reserved address space, resident only where it is touched, and pooled per worker
rules.diverges: concurrency costs a stack rather than a process, so one machine holds tasks in the hundred-thousands instead of workers in the hundreds

rules.title: A task's recursion limit is armed from the real bounds of the stack it was handed
rules.diverges: deep recursion throws a catchable error at a bound derived from the actual stack, rather than crashing the process or being counted by a configured depth alone

sections.title: What belongs in Core
sections.blurb: Core means always present. Six ordered tests place a candidate into one of five outcomes, and the roster records every one.

rules.title: `Core` means always present, so nothing outside Tier 0 may register a name under it
A library candidate is placed by six ordered tests, not by PHP's extension list
rules.diverges: PHP's extension partition tracks 1997 C build engineering and is not inherited — `ctype` and `str_pad` land in the same place

rules.title: A candidate lands in exactly one of five placements: Core, Native, Ext, Dropped or answered
Every subsystem's tier is recorded once in the roster, including the ones no milestone has built
The `Core` namespace is the compiler's: nothing may declare under it and its rosters are closed while compiling
rules.diverges: a misspelled built-in is a compile error naming the member rather than a run-time undefined-function fatal

rules.title: A domain class is a singular noun and its object types nest under it

sections.title: Naming and shape
sections.blurb: Twenty shape rules every member obeys: the subject first, a verb that predicts the return type, and casing that is a hard error.

rules.title: Every `Core` member obeys the same twenty shape rules, R1–R20
rules.diverges: PHP's built-ins have no API at all — argument order, failure signalling and option encoding vary between neighbouring functions in the same extension

rules.title: The subject is parameter 1 of every `Core` member, with no exceptions
rules.diverges: `array_map(f, a)` beside `array_filter(a, f)`, and `in_array`, `str_replace` and `preg_match` disagreeing about haystack-before-needle, all become one order

rules.title: A member's verb predicts its return type, and `…OrNull`, `…Safe`, `…Ex` and every `try…` but `tryParse` are banned
A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name, and which pair to reach for is a rule rather than taste
One name has one signature, and two behaviours need two names
A member name is a full word; only a class name may abbreviate, and only from a closed list
rules.diverges: `strlen` is `Core\Str::length`, not `Core\Str::len`

rules.title: An identifier's casing is fixed by its category and a mismatch is a hard compile error
rules.diverges: PHP checks legal characters and never case, so `snake_case` identifiers do not compile here

rules.title: Only the leading character's case is checked, so `HTTPClient` and `HttpClient` both pass
There is no suppression mechanism for a casing error, in any category
rules.diverges: unlike Rust's `#[allow(non_snake_case)]` there is no attribute, pragma or per-file opt-out; a name mirroring an external format is renamed or does not compile

sections.title: Everything is written down
sections.blurb: Visibility, wire-format participation and qualifier behaviour are all declared. Nothing about a member is inferred structurally.

rules.title: Every member declaration writes exactly one visibility keyword, and there is no implicit `public`
rules.diverges: `function f()`, `const X = 1`, `var $x;` and `readonly int $x;` all fail to compile — PHP's silent `public` has no successor

rules.title: An asymmetric property writes both halves, so a bare `private(set)` does not compile
rules.diverges: PHP 8.4 infers a `public` read side for a bare `private(set)`; that is the same implicit `public` in a different spelling and is refused

rules.title: `var $x;` and a bare `int $x;` in a class body report the missing visibility, not a statement error
A constructor parameter is not a member, because visibility is what promotes one
A class participates in a wire format only where it writes so, never structurally
rules.diverges: there is no `JsonSerializable`-style magic hook and no structural encoding of public properties

rules.title: Every `Core` member declares whether it is a sink, a launderer, contagious or neutral

sections.title: One way to do each thing
sections.blurb: Nothing mutates, nothing reads ambient state, no mutable twin, no mode string, no encoding argument, one range convention.

rules.title: No `Core` member mutates its argument and none takes a reference
rules.diverges: `sort($a)` becomes `$a = Arr::sort($a)`; there are no by-reference mutators, no out-parameters and no in-place variants

rules.title: Every `Core` value type is immutable, so no mutable twin exists to choose between
rules.diverges: there is no `DateTime`/`DateTimeImmutable` pair — one type, immutable

rules.title: No `Core` member reads ambient state: there is no default timezone, locale, array pointer or error global
rules.diverges: `setlocale`, `date_default_timezone_set`, the internal array pointer and every error global are absent; a `Zone` is an argument at every instant↔calendar conversion

rules.title: A `Core` member throws on failure and returns `?T` for absence; `false` is never an answer
rules.diverges: no member returns `false` to signal failure, no member returns an error code, and there is no `json_last_error` or `error_get_last`

rules.title: No operation is reachable two ways, and a domain class's statics never mirror an object's own methods
rules.diverges: the procedural twin of every OOP subsystem is gone — `date_*`, `collator_*`, the `fopen` family beside `SplFileObject`, `mysqli` twice

rules.title: A scalar and an `array<T>` never gain methods
rules.diverges: there is no `$s->length()` and no `$a->map()` — `Core\Str` and `Core\Arr` are the one spelling

rules.title: A mode is an enum, never a string or an integer constant, and only four grammars are exempt
rules.diverges: `fopen($p, "r+b")`, `hash("sha256", …)` and `MB_CASE_TITLE` have no spelling; a closed enum, or a subset of one, takes their place

rules.title: A unit is a type: a duration is a `Duration` and a size is `uint` bytes
rules.diverges: the `sleep`/`usleep`/`time_nanosleep` split does not exist — one parameter takes one `Duration`

rules.title: A `string` member never takes an encoding argument
Every range is `(offset, ?length)`, and a negative counts from the end

sections.title: Parameters and the options bag
sections.blurb: Optional knobs are one trailing shape literal — and required, optional and nullable stay three separate questions.

rules.title: A callback always receives `($value, $key)`, and may declare fewer parameters than the call site passes
rules.diverges: `ARRAY_FILTER_USE_KEY` and `ARRAY_FILTER_USE_BOTH` have nothing to select, and there is no `map`/`mapWithKey` pair

rules.title: Every `Core` parameter is callable by the name the spec writes, and that name is compatibility surface
A member's optional knobs are one trailing shape literal, never a flag or a bitmask
rules.diverges: there are no `bool` flag parameters, no `int` bitmask constants and no positional optional tail longer than one

rules.title: Required, optional and nullable are three separate questions: nullability belongs to the type and optionality to the default
rules.diverges: `?T` never means "the key may be absent", and there is no omit-when-null encoding option

rules.title: An options bag tells an omitted key from a written `null`
rules.diverges: PHP has no way to ask either question of an argument; here the two are different requests at every `Core` member

rules.title: A bag or shape field is nullable exactly when its omission fills the never-written marker
Wherever a `Core` member admits a written `null` it means remove, and `""` is never a removal spelling
rules.diverges: PHP spreads clearing across `unset`, `""`, `false` and per-function sentinels; here one spelling means one thing at every member

rules.title: The never-written marker is not in the type system and is never handed to user code
The three-state bag changes which constant fills a slot and nothing else about the ABI

sections.title: Shape parameters
sections.blurb: One checked type with disjoint arms, flattened away at the ABI so no shape exists at run time.

rules.title: Where the registry and the spec both describe an implemented member, precedence is field by field
A fixed-key shape parameter is one type carrying its arms, and it is only ever a whole parameter
A shape's arms are pairwise disjoint, so exactly one accepts a written literal and no field is declared a discriminant
The options bag and the shape parameter are two registry spellings of one checked type
A shape argument flattens into one argument per field of the merged list, so no shape exists at run time
A shape key reuses the options bag's two diagnostics, and a missing required key is an ordinary type mismatch

sections.title: Lifetimes, signatures and what is absent
sections.blurb: Anything with a lifetime is an object, a signature is taken over a payload, and every removed PHP built-in is accounted for by name.

rules.title: Anything with a lifetime is an object, and `Core` never hands back a handle
rules.diverges: there is no `resource`, no integer handle and no `$link`-first convention anywhere in `Core`

rules.title: A signature's lifetime is a required key and `null` is the forever spelling
A signature is taken over a structured payload, never over assembled text, and a URL is signed through the canonical form its class already defines
Every way of failing a signature check is one refusal, and expiry is the single distinguishable one
Two members are not a second spelling when each takes a different thing and answers a different thing
Cross-request state is reached through a member per tier, each with its own contract, never one API with a flag
rules.diverges: `apcu_*` and its shared-memory relatives are gone; the tier a program wants is the member it calls

rules.title: The whole temporary-file surface is one member handing out an owned directory
rules.diverges: `tmpfile`, `tempnam` and `sys_get_temp_dir` collapse into one member, and there is no `temporaryFile`

rules.title: The session roster is `start` and the members that work on the record it loaded, and a member called before `start` throws naming it
rules.diverges: `$_SESSION` does not exist and no member silently starts a session — `session_start` has to be written

rules.title: An implemented `Core` member carries its reference card in the registry declaration beside its code
A PHP built-in is absent for one of four standing reasons, and every removed name is accounted for by name
rules.diverges: roughly 1,900 built-ins become about 450 members covering strictly more ground

sections.title: Processes and files
sections.blurb: Running another program is argv only — there is no shell string anywhere — and a temporary directory sweeps itself.

rules.title: `Core\Cli::arguments` is how a program reads the words it was started with, at every depth
rules.diverges: `$argv` and `$argc` do not exist, the elements are `tainted`, and the answer is a process fact rather than a per-isolate one

rules.title: `Core\Script::args` is the value the current isolate was spawned with, and `null` where there was none
rules.diverges: Novis's own `$_ARGS` superglobal was retired for the same reason PHP's were — a spawned isolate reads its argument through a member

rules.title: `Core\Process` is the one way to run another program, and there is no shell string anywhere in it
rules.diverges: `exec`, `system`, `shell_exec`, `passthru`, `popen`, `proc_open` and backticks are all gone, and no flag brings a command line back

rules.title: `run` waits by suspending the coroutine, and hands back the exit code with both captures as `bytes`
rules.diverges: captured output is `bytes`, so text costs an `as string` that throws on invalid UTF-8 rather than mangling it

rules.title: `ProcessOptions` carries a working directory, a replaced environment and a timeout, and nothing else
rules.diverges: a supplied environment replaces the parent's rather than merging with it

rules.title: `spawn` answers a handle whose reads and writes suspend, covering `proc_open` and `passthru` in one type
A target only a second command-line parser could run is refused, on every platform
rules.diverges: a `.bat`, `.cmd` or `.ps1` target does not run at all; a shebang script does, because `execve` reads it without re-parsing anything

rules.title: `Core\IO::writeStream` is where every stream reaches disk, and a failed write removes its partial file
rules.diverges: there is no `move_uploaded_file` and no temp file to move — a part is streamed to a path the program chose, and `overwrite` defaults to false

rules.title: A temporary directory lives under a Novis-owned root and is deleted when its script ends, and the sweep never throws
rules.diverges: there is no `tmpfile`, no `sys_get_temp_dir` writing and no `tempnam` — the runtime hands out a directory it owns and reclaims it

rules.title: The orphan sweep is keyed on the owner being alive, never on age, and runs in exactly two places

sections.title: Regex, HTML and introspection
sections.blurb: A two-tier regex engine, auto-escaping output with one typed bypass, read-only reflection, and an inert parse tree.

rules.title: A pattern runs on the linear engine unless it cannot, and the backtracking tier's step budget throws when exhausted
rules.diverges: there is no modifier that asks for backtracking, and `preg_*`'s silent `false` on a backtrack limit is a catchable throw here

rules.title: A literal pattern is validated and tiered while checking, and a malformed one is a compile error
Regex syntax is PCRE's with no `u` modifier, and a construct neither engine supports is diagnosed by name
rules.diverges: Unicode mode is not a flag because `string` is always UTF-8, and `/e` and its relatives are not reintroduced

rules.title: `echo` in an HTTP request escapes everything it is given, and `Core\Html\Markup` is the only raw-write bypass
rules.diverges: output is escaped by the sink rather than by a call the developer remembers, and a runtime-computed string can never become `Markup` through `as`

rules.title: ``html`…` `` is a `Core\Html\Markup` whose segments are trusted and whose holes are escaped
rules.diverges: there is no template literal in PHP; the nearest thing is `<?= ?>` in an inline-HTML region, and this is that rule available in expression position

rules.title: `Core\Html::escape` answers a `Markup`, so the eager-escape habit stops compiling
rules.diverges: `htmlspecialchars`'s replacement does not answer a `string`, so its result cannot be concatenated back into one and double-escaped

rules.title: `Core\Html::toSource` is the one way out of a `Markup`, and it takes a written reason
`Core\Html::sanitize` answers a `Markup` by rebuilding the document, never by filtering it
HTML parses by the WHATWG algorithm onto `Core\Xml`'s own tree, and that parse never fails
rules.diverges: there is no `LIBXML_*` flag matrix and no document class that flips between recovering and throwing — the two front doors are two classes

rules.title: `Core\Xml` is a materialising tree beside a one-window stream, and no operation is available through both
rules.diverges: `DOMDocument`, `SimpleXMLElement`, `XMLReader` and the expat callbacks are four vocabularies for one document — there are two here, they share a node family, and they share no operation

rules.title: `Core\Xml` refuses a document type declaration whole and resolves no entity, so XXE and billion-laughs are absent rather than bounded
rules.diverges: there is no `libxml_disable_entity_loader`, no `LIBXML_NOENT` and no entity loader for either to have switched — a `<!DOCTYPE …>` does not parse at all

rules.title: `Core\Validate` carries no predicate that names a type, because `as ?T` already is one
rules.diverges: `is_numeric`, `ctype_digit`, `filter_var(FILTER_VALIDATE_INT)` and their kind have no replacement — the conversion is the test

rules.title: `Core\Secret::reveal` is the one named way out of `secret`, and it carries a written reason
rules.diverges: there is no generic unwrap; a confidential value leaves its qualifier only through this member or through a function that consumes it and returns something else

rules.title: `Core\Reflect` is read-only structural introspection, and it is a first-class feature rather than an extension
rules.diverges: reflection is always present rather than a compiled-in extension, it covers no traits because there are none, and it never widens access

rules.title: `Core\Ast` runs the compiler's own parser and hands back typed, inert nodes
rules.diverges: `token_get_all`'s untyped arrays are replaced by one type per production, and there is no `eval` for a rewritten tree to reach

rules.title: `Core\Topic` is the only way two connections meet, and a slow subscriber is closed rather than tolerated

sections.title: Connecting to a database
sections.blurb: One database API, every statement prepared, three deny-by-default capabilities, and defaults that close what PHP leaves open.

rules.title: `Core\Db` is the only database API, and every statement it runs is prepared
rules.diverges: there is no PDO, no mysqli, no pgsql and no sqlite3 twin, no `quote`/`real_escape_string`, no emulated prepares and no multi-statement query

rules.title: A connection is named in configuration or built from settings, and both memoize for the request
rules.diverges: a credential is never a DSN string in program source, and there is no destructor to close a connection — the request teardown does it

rules.title: Three deny-by-default capabilities gate naming a database, dialling one, and issuing DDL to it
rules.diverges: opening a connection is a granted act rather than a library call, and a hostname reaching `Settings.host` may not be `tainted`

rules.title: Three connection defaults close holes PHP leaves open, and none can be configured to the unsafe value
rules.diverges: `LOCAL INFILE` cannot be enabled, TLS verifies fully rather than `prefer`, and the charset is forced to UTF-8

rules.title: The five drivers are an enum with one `match` per entry point, not a `Driver` trait
A Unix-socket host is the string that deployment already holds, and MSSQL refuses one
`serverVersion` answers what the server said during the handshake, and never spends a round trip
Busy state is a field on the connection, and a wire not at a message boundary is closed rather than reset
Five members run a statement, results are buffered by default, and only one of them streams
rules.diverges: there is no unbuffered-query flag and no per-driver difference in what a second statement on a busy connection does

sections.title: Running a statement
sections.blurb: One placeholder is one value. Columns have natural types, transactions are closures, and one error kind spans every driver.

rules.title: One placeholder is one value, and expanding a list into `IN` is written with `Core\Db::inList`
rules.diverges: an array bound to a placeholder is one value rather than a silently expanded list, and an empty `inList` throws instead of guessing

rules.title: A literal query is checked while compiling, and no vendor's SQL grammar is ever parsed
Every column has one natural Novis type, and the requested type converts losslessly or throws
rules.diverges: nothing is a string because the text protocol made it one — a `DECIMAL` is a `decimal`, a `BIGINT UNSIGNED` is a `uint`, and `TINYINT(1)` holding `7` refuses to read as `bool`

rules.title: A streaming result holds its connection until it is drained, and a second statement on it throws
A stream's read state is parked on the connection on every driver, and a buffer is never the answer
A transaction is a closure, and `Transaction` is a `Queryable` rather than a second query surface
rules.diverges: there is no `beginTransaction`/`commit`/`rollBack` on the connection and no `inTransaction`; nesting is a savepoint, and a rollback signal survives an intervening `catch (Throwable)`

rules.title: One `DbError` carries a normalised kind across every driver, and never a bound parameter
rules.diverges: an application branches on `ErrorKind::UniqueViolation` rather than on `1062`, `23505` or the text `"Duplicate entry"`

rules.title: The wire lives in `nvs-db` below the standard library, where a codec is borrowed and a state machine is written

sections.title: Schemas and convergence
sections.blurb: A schema is a value, a plan is its difference from a live database, and something the schema omits is reported, never dropped.

rules.title: A schema is a value with three spellings, and its array form is the canonical one
The schema vocabulary is five constructs shared by all five backends, with no raw escape hatch
A unique key reads nulls as distinct on every backend, and SQL Server spells that as a filtered index
A plan is the difference between a schema value and a live database, and `Core` knows no migrations
rules.diverges: there is no version number, no history table, no `up`/`down` pair and no fleet lock — the plan is recomputed from the database every time

rules.title: An existing database is read by catalog query, and no DDL parser exists at any tier
Every plan step carries a grade and its complete SQL, and an unknown grade grades up
Something in the database and not in the schema value is reported with its SQL, and never dropped
Planning is an ordinary read, and applying takes `db.schema` under a member named for its risk

sections.title: Codecs, sessions, rate limits and signatures
sections.blurb: One attribute generates a codec from the declared property list; sessions start explicitly; both rate-limit verbs are their own job.

rules.title: One written attribute per format generates a codec, and it is matched by resolved name
rules.diverges: no class is serialisable by being a class — a wire format is opted into at the declaration, and visibility never decides what is encoded

rules.title: The field list is the declared property list, and every field is a constructor parameter of the same name
A generated decoder reports every failed field at once, before the constructor runs
rules.diverges: a decode failure is one throw carrying a located list, not the first problem the parser happened to hit

rules.title: The derive generates only the half the class does not write, at compile time, storing nothing per object
The job queue is two tables in a connection the operator names, converged by an explicit command
rules.diverges: there is no broker, no daemon of its own and no implicit boot-time DDL — the tables are created by `nvs queue migrate` and by nothing else

rules.title: A session is opened by calling `Core\Session::start`, and there is no ambient session array
rules.diverges: `$_SESSION` does not exist, nothing starts a session implicitly, and a member called before `start` throws

rules.title: `consume` and `shed` are two jobs with two verbs, and neither is a tier of the other
rules.diverges: there is no per-IP or per-path limiting, no `[ratelimit]` config block and no middleware writing a `429` for you

rules.title: Both tiers run GCRA over one stored timestamp per key, and the `Decision` computes `retryAfter`
An unreachable shared store throws, because whether to fail open is knowledge only the call site has
`Core\Crypto`'s algorithm roster is closed, every algorithm argument is required, and the sealed layout is what a browser reads
rules.diverges: there is no cipher name in a string and no unauthenticated mode to reach for, so `aes-256-ecb` has no spelling

rules.title: `Core\Signature` signs a canonicalized payload, and the lifetime rides inside the signed bytes
rules.diverges: there is no string to assemble and therefore nothing for two sides to disagree about, and a verified payload comes back `tainted`

rules.title: `Core\Router` signs a route name and its parameters, so a signature survives a remount

sections.title: URIs and images
sections.blurb: An image is an immutable value carrying a plan — nothing decodes until a terminal runs it, under a cap read off the header.

rules.title: `Core\Uri` spends the omitted-versus-null distinction on three components and on one query parameter at a time
rules.diverges: there is no `parse_url`/`http_build_query` round trip to lose a component in — removing one is a written `null`, and an empty query is a different value from no query

rules.title: A member whose output scales with its input either allocates through the guarded value allocator or bounds the input
Every decompression runs under an output ceiling and a ratio, and there is no spelling for turning either off
rules.diverges: `$max_length` was optional and defaulted to unlimited, so the safe call was the one the caller had to remember to write

rules.title: An image is an immutable value carrying a plan, and nothing decodes until a terminal runs it
rules.diverges: gd's mutable resource and its ambient mode flags are gone; an operation answers a new value, and the component's entry points are coarse by rule

rules.title: Pixels are RGBA8 and nothing else, which retires gd's palettes, mode flags and drawing primitives
rules.diverges: there are no palette images, no `imagesetpixel`, no drawing primitives and no `imageaffine` — four named transforms cover the affine cases a web application reaches for

rules.title: The format roster is a closed table of decoders and encoders, each naming what implements it
rules.diverges: TIFF, BMP, TGA, ICO, PNM, HEIC and gd's own formats are not readable at all, and JPEG XL decodes without encoding

rules.title: The pixel cap is read off the header before a buffer is allocated, and a call may only lower it
rules.diverges: a decompression bomb is refused from its declared dimensions rather than discovered by exhausting memory

rules.title: `open` orients and converts to sRGB, and `encode` strips metadata unless the plan kept it
rules.diverges: a phone photo is upright and a CMYK JPEG is sRGB without the caller knowing the tags exist, and location data does not survive a re-encode

rules.title: Comparison, hashing, placeholders, text, QR codes and SVG are one entry point each, because each is one job

sections.title: PDF and spreadsheets
sections.blurb: Two first-party extensions that perform no I/O and write nothing a reader would execute, byte-identical for equal input.

rules.title: PDF generation is a first-party extension that performs no I/O, and an unresolved asset throws
rules.diverges: the SSRF and local-file-read class that defines PHP's HTML-to-PDF libraries is absent by construction — there is nothing in the sandbox to fetch with

rules.title: The only input language is HTML plus a CSS subset, and every backend answers that one interface
rules.diverges: there is no second FPDF-shaped imperative engine with its own coordinate model — drawings are inline SVG

rules.title: The CSS subset is documented, and the render result lists every declaration it dropped
The writer emits nothing a reader would execute, and equal input gives byte-equal output
A PDF page is a decode-only format of the image component: one page per `open`, priced by the pixel cap
rules.diverges: rasterising a page needs no Imagick, no Ghostscript and no shell — it is `Image::open` with a `page` and a `dpi`

rules.title: An encrypted document and a detectable omission both throw, and everything past rasterising is somebody else's job
The spreadsheet component is a first-party extension that fetches nothing and executes nothing it reads
rules.diverges: an external workbook reference, a linked image and a remote data connection come back as data, and VBA is enumerable payload that never runs

rules.title: Only an explicit `Formula` value writes a formula cell, so an export built from user data is inert
rules.diverges: a string beginning `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` writes as text, so formula injection is closed by type rather than by a remembered quote prefix

rules.title: A workbook crosses the boundary in whole blocks, and a bomb is refused before a sheet buffer exists
rules.diverges: there is no per-cell accessor to loop over, which is the shape most PhpSpreadsheet code takes

rules.title: The roster is read-wide and write-narrow, a macro is never written, and evaluation is an explicit call
The writer embeds no executable content and no entropy, so equal input gives byte-equal output
`Core\Net` is one class over TCP, UDP and Unix sockets, reached through five entry points that park on the runtime's own reactor
A `Core\Net` socket closes with the request that opened it, so there is no persistent connection and no pool across requests
A datagram socket sends and receives messages and offers no ordering, retransmission or acknowledgement above them

sections.title: Metrics
sections.blurb: Three verbs for three kinds, nine series that exist the moment an exporter is configured, and a name fixed to one kind for good.

rules.title: Production telemetry is read from the instrumentation that already exists, and adds no probe site to the measured path
rules.diverges: there is no APM extension in the request path and no userland StatsD or OpenTelemetry client to reconcile with it; the runtime's own probes are the only instrumentation

rules.title: A trace id exists for every request whatever the sampling decision, and it is the only request identifier
rules.diverges: there is no `X-Request-ID` read or minted; the W3C trace id is the request identifier a log line, an error rendering and a proxy all share

rules.title: A log record inside an active trace carries `trace_id` and `span_id`, and outside one omits both rather than writing them empty
rules.diverges: `error_log` writes no correlation id; every JSON-Lines record written inside a traced request can be joined to its trace from the line alone

rules.title: `Core\Metrics` is three verbs for three kinds, always present, and accumulates whether or not an exporter is built
rules.diverges: there is no client library to install and no `record(name, value, kind)`; a counter, a histogram and a gauge are three members, and a name is validated at a literal call site

rules.title: Ten series exist the moment an exporter is configured, with no application code written
rules.diverges: request rate, latency, query time, GC pause and spawn overhead are on the scrape endpoint before the application emits anything, where PHP needs an APM agent or a hand-written StatsD client for the first three and cannot reach the last two at all

rules.title: A metric name is fixed to one kind and one label set on first use, and a second kind throws naming both sites
rules.diverges: recording one name as a counter here and a gauge there is a throw at the second call, not a series the backend quietly reports twice

rules.title: The `route` label carries the route's declared name, never the request path, and a route without one has no label
rules.diverges: a series is keyed by the route's compiled name rather than by the request path a StatsD client would key on, so `/users/1`, `/users/2` is one series and not one per user

rules.title: A metrics registry is per core, merged at scrape, and no program reads a metric
rules.diverges: there is no APCu-style shared counter store; every core keeps its own approximate aggregate and the merge is arithmetic at scrape time

rules.title: Past `max_series` a new series is refused and an existing one is never evicted
rules.diverges: past the cap the newest label set is dropped with a warning, not the oldest evicted; a counter never appears to reset

rules.title: `[metrics]` and `[trace]` are `System` blocks, and a value neither exporter accepts is refused at boot
rules.diverges: a request cannot switch tracing on for itself the way `xdebug_start_trace()` or an `ini_set` can; where telemetry ships is the deployment's decision

sections.title: Traces and spans
sections.blurb: Exactly four things become a span, an inbound `traceparent` is continued, and sampling is decided once at the root.

rules.title: Exactly four things become a span, and a `call` event never does
rules.diverges: a distributed trace is not Xdebug's per-call function trace; a span is a request, a query, an outbound call or a spawn, and nothing finer

rules.title: A `call` event never becomes a span; the root, a `query`, an outbound HTTP call and a `spawn` do, and `gc` becomes a metric
rules.diverges: an OpenTelemetry SDK installed as a library lets a program open a span around any function; here the set of things that become a span is closed and a function call is not in it

rules.title: A trace event carries one of five kinds — `call`, `gc`, `spawn`, `query`, `http` — and a `call` keeps its probe shape
rules.diverges: Xdebug's trace is a log of function calls; here a collector pause, an isolate spawn and a database statement are events of their own on the same stream, tagged so a viewer can tell them apart

rules.title: A statement is a `query` trace event that carries its duration, driver, connection, truncated SQL and row counts, and never a bound parameter
rules.diverges: there are no mysqlnd statistics and no general query log; a statement is a trace event, filed in the driver and off the hot path, and it never carries a bound value

rules.title: A `[db.<name>] slow_query` threshold writes a statement's span facts to `Core\Log`, and is off until a block writes one
rules.diverges: the slow-query log is a per-connection threshold in `nvs.toml` written by the application's operator, not the server's `slow_query_log`, and it reports the same facts the trace does

rules.title: A collector pause is a `gc` event recorded from the collector's run routine, never from the safepoint poll
A spawn and its join are one `spawn` event naming the form it was, with an overhead split where the child reports its own time, and a child's own stream never crosses live
An inbound `traceparent` is continued, and one the process cannot read starts a new trace rather than failing the request
`Core\Http\Client` sends `traceparent` while `[trace] propagate` is on, and the id it sends is the request's own
rules.diverges: a trace crosses a service boundary with no header code in the application, where a PHP client has to be wrapped to carry one

rules.title: Sampling is decided once at the root by `[trace] sample`, and an inbound trace that is already sampled is always continued
The exporter is a feature-gated Native subsystem, and `Core\Metrics` is Tier 0 in every build
The OTLP and Prometheus paths are somebody else's specification, implemented here; the wiring and the registry are ours
An exporter brings no second registry, no second scheduler and no second client, and a crate is taken only for an encoder
The four event kinds export as one speedscope evented timeline, beside Callgrind, Clover/lcov and NDJSON
rules.diverges: there is no Xdebug cachegrind file to open in a bespoke viewer; the timeline is speedscope's open evented format, the same file the sampling profiler writes

rules.title: A request reads its own memory as `memoryHeld`, `memoryPeak` and `memoryLimit` on `Core\Budget`, and the process's resident bytes are `Core\Os`'s
rules.diverges: there is no `$real_usage` boolean and no second accounting behind it: `memory_get_usage`'s two numbers were one member with a flag, where the request's held bytes and the process's resident set are two members on the two classes that own them

rules.title: The runtime records a request's memory high-water mark in every build, and a nested isolate restores the enclosing mark rather than clobbering it
rules.diverges: `memory_get_peak_usage` reads a mark PHP keeps because its allocator holds its chunks; here the mark is kept deliberately, because deterministic release means the current figure falls back to the baseline and hides the spike

rules.title: A `[limits] memory_high_water` fraction writes one `Warn` when a request's memory peak crosses that share of its ceiling, and is off until a block writes one
rules.diverges: PHP has no warning short of the fatal: a request that touched 96% of `memory_limit` and returned successfully is indistinguishable from one that never passed 30%

sections.title: Exit hooks
sections.blurb: A request-local hook that observes how the request ended and never steers it — and the two endings that fire no hook at all.

rules.title: `Core\Script::onExit` registers a request-local hook that runs FIFO as the last user code, and each hook receives one readonly `ExitReport`
rules.diverges: `register_shutdown_function` is gone; the hook takes a typed `Script\ExitReport` with the reason, the status and the live `Throwable`, where PHP reads `error_get_last()`

rules.title: The exit queue drains once — at a normal end, at `exit` and at an uncaught throw — and the report says which ending it was
Exit hooks run after every `finally` and after the failure hooks, and before native teardown, with the heap alive and output where it was
A `FATAL` and a cancellation run no exit hook — `Core\Fatal::onLimit` is the one observer of a limit breach
rules.diverges: PHP's shutdown functions fire on most fatals; here a resource-limit `FATAL` reaches only `Core\Fatal::onLimit`, and a migrator moves that one use there

rules.title: A hook observes the ending and never steers it: the report is fixed first, a throw is logged and abandoned, `exit` inside a hook throws, and the drain continues
rules.diverges: a shutdown function in PHP can call `exit` to change the status or silently swallow the pending error; here neither is possible

sections.title: Listening and admission
sections.blurb: What the server is and is not, how mounts expand at boot, and the valve that answers 503 before an isolate exists.

rules.title: The server is a development server or a proxied production origin, and nothing a proxy does earlier is in it
rules.diverges: there is no php-fpm and no FastCGI: the origin speaks HTTP/1.1 over TCP or a Unix socket, terminates no TLS and compresses nothing, so nginx's `fastcgi_pass` becomes `proxy_pass`

rules.title: Only `listen`, `socket_mode` and `workers` in `[server]` need a restart, `listen` is one flat array defaulting to `127.0.0.1:8000` in both modes, and the flag is the last word
rules.diverges: `listen` is the origin's own address rather than a php-fpm pool's, and `workers` counts accept cores rather than sizing a `pm.*` process pool

rules.title: A mount matches on `prefix` or `host`, names one `entry` or one `scan`, and a scan expands against the disk at boot and again whenever a scanned directory changes
rules.diverges: a vhost's rewrite rules become one `[[server.mount]]` block, and a module is relocatable because the matched prefix is stripped before the route table sees the path

rules.title: A mount's key set is `prefix`, `host`, `scan`, `entry` and `origin`; `mode`, limits and capabilities belong to the `[[app]]` block
`nvs serve` needs no file over a written mount table, serves that table whole under the global configuration, and refuses a start that names nothing
A `listen` entry beginning with a separator is a Unix socket, Unix-only, with `socket_mode`, and it is the transport a proxy should prefer
rules.diverges: the same `listen = /run/nvs.sock` shape as php-fpm, but a Windows host has no named-pipe equivalent and listens on TCP loopback

rules.title: `[mode] ceiling` is `System`-class, bounds a runtime flip and not the startup value, and unset equals the mode the server started in
rules.diverges: there is no `php.ini-development` to copy: a production host that wrote nothing is unreachable from code, and one root-owned line opens it

rules.title: A development-mode server binding a non-loopback address prints a banner, writes one `Warn` record naming the address, and serves
rules.diverges: `php -S 0.0.0.0:8000` says nothing; here the bind is announced on the console and in the log stream, and it is not refused

rules.title: A default that is unsafe inbound or unbounded outbound is a defect, not a neutral starting point
rules.diverges: php-fpm behind nginx ships no security headers, no cookie flags and no outbound timeout until somebody writes them; here nothing written is already the safe and finite configuration

rules.title: Every `[server] listen` entry is bound before any core accepts, each core holds its own handle on every listener, and `[server] workers` bounds the count over the machine's available parallelism
rules.diverges: php-fpm sizes a pool of request *processes* with `pm.*`; `workers` counts accept cores, and one core answers many requests at once

rules.title: `max_in_flight` is a process-wide valve that answers a fixed `503` with `Retry-After` before an isolate exists
rules.diverges: php-fpm's `pm.max_children` queues on the socket and the proxy reports a 504; here the origin answers `503` with `Retry-After: 1` itself, and no custom error page runs

rules.title: The effective in-flight ceiling is the smaller of `max_in_flight` and what the memory budget affords, and a clamp is logged at boot and by every reload
rules.diverges: `pm.max_children` is a free number and the out-of-memory killer enforces its product with memory; here the ceiling is derived from the budget, the configured number is clamped rather than trusted, and the overflow is a `503`
